I’m honored to represent Washington’s 1st District in Congress. I’m focused on working to move past the rhetoric in Washington, D.C., and deliver results for the working families and businesses of the 1st District. It’s time we have leaders in Washington, D.C. that put people above politics, and have the experience and determination to help create jobs and build an economy that works for all. I hope you will join me. Please use this website for the latest news and updates from the campaign.
If your intention was to visit my official House of Representatives website, please click here .
Creating an economy that works for everyone.

pages.title: Issues - Delbene For Congress
paragraphs: We’re at a critical juncture in our country today. Too many issues have gone unaddressed for too long, hurting our economy and working families. We can’t afford to play partisan games or keep the same failed policies that created these problems in the first place. I support expanding economic opportunity, helping working families and small businesses, spurring job growth, and being fiscally responsible. I am focused on results, not rhetoric.

While our economy grew because of Democrats’ economic policies, including the expansion of the Child Tax Credit, under the Trump administration many families are struggling with rising costs including the price of gas, housing, and child care. I’m committed to creating an economy that works for everyone.

In the time he’s been back in office, Trump has brazenly violated the law, threatened the safety of our communities, and jeopardized our country’s economic security. I am fighting every single day as Chair of the DCCC to win us a majority in November 2026, so that we can hold this administration accountable.

We cannot go back to the days when someone could be denied coverage because of a pre-existing condition or when you could be charged more for coverage for simply being a woman. That’s why I have consistently voted to protect the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and build on it. I support getting America to universal quality coverage and the best way to incentivize competition is to give people a choice between public and private coverage options.

We must fix our nation’s broken immigration system so it works for families, businesses, and our economy. We must pass comprehensive immigration reform which I have championed since being sworn in to Congress and we need legal guardrails to prevent ICE from committing violence and terrorizing our communities.

The Pacific Northwest is already experiencing the impacts of climate change. Growing wildfire seasons and changing ocean conditions harm our communities and environment. We need meaningful action now to combat climate change to protect our health, wellbeing, and natural resources.

I support investing in proven community policing and crime diversion programs to keep our streets, homes, and communities safe. We can both invest in our local police forces and demand accountability from those we count on to protect us. We must also address the endemic gun violence in America so our families and communities are safe.

An extreme Republican supermajority on the Supreme Court has now stripped women of their constitutional right to an abortion. I’m a strong supporter of the Women’s Health Protection Act, a bill to guarantee everyone access to abortion care no matter which state they live in. I’m also fighting for strong, commonsense policies that address the economic challenges facing women and families.

Hundreds of thousands of Americans across the country lack access to safe, affordable housing. More than 12 million households in America pay more than half of their income in rent, while many others find housing completely out of reach—leaving them without a stable roof over their head, and often forcing them to sleep on the streets. This is unacceptable.

Social Security has been a building block of our middle class and a secure retirement. It’s created a social safety net and basic financial security for seniors. It’s an investment we’ve all made and a promise I’m committed to protecting and strengthening for all of our seniors.

Investing in our infrastructure is how we keep our economy moving. In the last year, I’ve secured funding for fifteen projects, totaling more than $21.5 million invested in the 1st Congressional District.

Trump has recklessly tried to shutter the Department of Education. I strongly oppose his illegal attempt to dismantle the department, which would slash federal funding for public schools nationwide, eliminate programs for children with disabilities, and cut programs that make attending college affordable. Let’s be clear, eliminating the Department of Education would require an act of Congress – and I will fight any effort to do so.

Fighting to protect the privacy of all of us means your personal information is protected from private entities and public ones. It’s why when President Trump gave Elon Musk and the ‘Department of Government Efficiency’ unprecedented access to your sensitive personal, financial, and health information with little oversight or accountability – it was outrageous and illegal.

pages.title: Economic Security and Rising Costs for Families - Delbene For Congress
paragraphs: Economic Security and Rising Costs for Families

While our economy grew because of Democrats’ economic policies, including the expansion of the Child Tax Credit, under the Trump administration many families are struggling with rising costs including the price of gas, housing, and child care. I’m committed to creating an economy that works for everyone by helping our small businesses and local industries rebuild so they can support good-paying jobs for years to come, including in the aerospace, manufacturing, high-tech, sustainable agriculture, clean energy, and health care industries. We must support businesses that are creating jobs and invest in the training, education, and skills of our workers to ensure they are prepared for success. This has been a long-term commitment of mine since I secured $200 million to expand job training opportunities during my first term in Congress.

Whether at the grocery store, the pharmacy counter, or the gas pump, everything is getting more expensive. But Republicans in D.C. not only refuse to take action to provide meaningful relief, they have made things worse. Tariffs are raising costs across the board, whether it’s food, clothing, or even school supplies! The Republican Big, Ugly Bill is driving up utility bills across the country. Republican cuts to Medicaid and their refusal to extend tax credits under the Affordable Care Act are spiking health care costs and ripping away health care coverage from millions.
Donald Trump and Republicans promised to lower costs on ‘day one.’ Since Trump returned to office, it’s been nothing but one big broken promise.

Washington families and businesses have suffered due to Trump’s illegal and indiscriminate use of tariffs – raising prices on everything, on everyone. As one of the most trade dependent states in the nation, Trump’s tariffs have had a damaging impact on countless Washington businesses by raising input costs and closing off markets. I have been a leader in asserting Congress’s Constitutional authority when it comes to trade policy and have introduced several bills to curb Trump’s abuses of power, including the Prevent Tariff Abuse Act and the Congressional Trade Authority Act. I also provided arguments to the Supreme Court which ultimately aligned with the high court’s decision to strike down Trump’s illegal tariffs.

I am an original cosponsor of the RELIEF Act, which would require the federal government to automatically refund tariffs and customs duties collected under Trump’s illegal tariffs. I am also an original cosponsor of legislation that would repeal Section 122 to prevent further tariff abuse by Trump .

As a member of the tax-writing Ways and Means Committee, I am focused on modernizing the tax code and creating policies that are fair for all Americans and give businesses the ability to plan for the future. Tax policy should focus on growing the middle class and providing economic opportunity. Through a modernized tax code, we can also invest more in America, encouraging job creation and innovation. Congress should focus on simplifying our tax code by eliminating inefficient and unfair tax breaks and subsidies that no longer make sense in today’s global economy. Any time our federal government offers a tax break or subsidy, we should consider it as an investment and evaluate whether we are getting an adequate return. We must also stop governing retroactively and with short-term policies that Congress must extend each year. Families and businesses need predictability and stability.

Under the Republican majority in the House, none of this has happened. Instead of modernizing the tax code to help working families and spur economic growth, Republicans passed their Big, Ugly Bill which gave massive tax breaks to the wealthiest few while gutting health care, only to increase the federal deficit by trillions over the next decade.

We need a Congress that will focus on putting working families and broad economic growth first, and that’s what I’m fighting for every day. I continue to champion efforts that provide tax relief for the middle-class, including the enhanced Child Tax Credit and the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit. The enhanced Child Tax Credit was included in the American Rescue Plan and provided families with monthly checks for 6 months and lifted 3 million kids out of poverty. I am also the lead sponsor of legislation that would create or preserve more than 2 million affordable housing units nationwide in the next decade and address the growing housing crisis.

The President has plunged us into a reckless war in Iran that has cost American lives, billions of dollars, and destabilized the Middle East and global markets. He’s done all of this without articulating a strategy with clear objectives and has not made the case to the American public for the justification for his war of choice. Congress has the sole authority to declare war. I have voted in favor of multiple War Powers Resolutions directing the removal of the U.S. Armed forces from hostilities within or against Venezuela and from hostilities with Iran. I continue to oppose rogue presidential military operations and will do everything possible to ensure that the American people are not drawn into forever wars.

pages.title: Holding the Administration Accountable - Delbene For Congress
paragraphs: In the time he’s been back in office, Trump has brazenly violated the law, threatened the safety of our communities, and jeopardized our country’s economic security. I am fighting every single day as Chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) to win us a majority in November 2026, so that we can hold this administration accountable.

Once Democrats re-take the majority, we will reassert Congress’s constitutional authority, including the subpoena power that the Republican majority has surrendered to Trump. As a member of the Ways & Means Oversight Subcommittee, I will help lead a Democratic majority in holding this administration accountable and provide transparency to the American people.

I have fought back against Trump’s reckless war of choice in Iran, led the fight against his illegal tariffs, and stood against giving ICE a blank check. I will continue to fight for real reforms to the out of control agency.

When Trump attempted to unlawfully halt federal grants in order to advance his agenda during his first weeks in office, I fought to stop these reckless actions that would have caused significant harm to our communities. In less than 24 hours, he was forced to lift his blanket freeze on the funds.

I have consistently spoken out against attempts to disenfranchise voters, including both versions of the so-called “SAVE Act” which would undermine eligible voters’ constitutional right to vote and infringe on their data.

The Supreme Court decision in Louisiana v. Callais is just the latest example of Trump and Republicans attempts to rig the midterms. The decision shows the need for national legislation to protect the rights of all voters, end these mid-decade gerrymanders, and the far-right’s assault on the Voting Rights Act. I am an original cosponsor and loud advocate for the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to do just that.
If Republicans try to dismantle seats or erode our rights – we’ll fight back. In the courthouse, the statehouse, and at the ballot box.

Some of Trump’s most egregious acts include his Executive Order to end birthright citizenship, the mass layoffs of federal workers with no regard for the impact on the services and the programs that the American taxpayer depends on, and the termination of hundreds of billions of federal grants that fund lifesaving research and critical infrastructure projects to keep America’s economy moving.

In response, I have fought back in the courts. I have provided arguments to the courts in over 30 cases, seeking to protect the 14th Amendment, unfreeze hundreds of billions of dollars of federal grants, overturn illegal tariffs, preserve the jobs of tens of thousands of federal employees living and working in Washington State, and protect women’s access to reproductive care.

As Chair of the DCCC, I have also fought tirelessly against Trump’s redistricting schemes. He and his MAGA majority know they can’t win on the issues, so they are trying everything they can to rig the midterms. We’ve taken action in courts across the country on everything from redistricting to campaign finance.

pages.title: Health Care - Delbene For Congress
paragraphs: We cannot go back to the days when someone could be denied coverage because of a pre-existing condition or when you could be charged more for coverage for simply being a woman. That’s why I have consistently voted to protect the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and build on it. I championed the passage of the American Rescue Plan in 2021, which included the first major expansion of the advanced premium tax credits since the ACA’s initial passage, which helped nearly 22 million people across the country enroll in affordable, quality health care. However, Congressional Republicans let these tax credits expire at the end of 2025. Because Congress failed to extend them, Washingtonians enrolled in health plans through WA Healthplanfinder are seeing their premiums increase by an average of 65 percent. This will cause tens of thousands of Washingtonians to lose their health care coverage.

I am working to ensure the ACA tax credits are permanent. In January 2026, House Democrats fought for legislation to extend them for three years. While this effort passed the House of Representatives, Republicans in the Senate stalled this effort, leaving many Americans with rising health care costs. The fight isn’t over, and I’m still working everyday to restore this critical program.

I support getting America to universal quality coverage and the best way to incentivize competition is to give people a choice between public and private coverage options. We must make it easier and more affordable for small businesses to provide health coverage for their employees.

Medicaid, called Apple Health in Washington, along with the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) provide coverage to nearly 80 million people nationwide, including more than 1.8 million Washingtonians. These programs play a crucial role in providing families access to health care. However, the Republican’s Big, Ugly Bill, gave substantial tax cuts to the wealthiest Americans and paid for them by slashing Medicaid funding by $1 trillion. These cuts include at least $3 billion from Apple Health each year. We must reverse these cruel, Republican cuts to Medicaid when Democrats take back the House Majority.

Medicare is a cornerstone of our nation’s health care system. I am committed to protecting it and will fight against any efforts to privatize or dismantle Medicare. The focus instead should be on controlling the rising costs of care and improving the quality of care our seniors receive. That’s why I championed policies that now allow the government to negotiate lower prescription drug prices in Medicare, cap insulin prices at $35 per month, and cap out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors at $2,000 annually. These commonsense reforms are costs for seniors and improve access to care. Moving forward, we must extend these hard-fought cost savings to all Americans, not just those with Medicare.

During my time in Congress, I have focused on making health care work better for patients and providers. That is why I introduced the Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act to streamline health insurance red tape to deliver quality care faster. Due to the overwhelming bipartisan support for my legislation, the federal government implemented many elements of the bill, and I am now focused on cementing that policy into law so that insurance plans will be held accountable for delaying or denying medically necessary care that seniors are entitled to.

I am also leading the charge against a new program the Trump administration started this year in Washington and five other states that allows private companies to use AI to delay and deny care for seniors on traditional Medicare and pays the company based on how much care they deny. I introduced the Seniors Deserve SMARTER Care Act to cancel the program.

pages.title: Immigration - Delbene For Congress
paragraphs: We must fix our nation’s broken immigration system so it works for families, businesses, and our economy.

Immigration reform is especially important for Washington state. We have a vibrant agricultural industry, world-leading technology, and advanced manufacturing businesses. Workers, families, students, and entrepreneurs are all hurting because our current system is so dysfunctional. Business, labor, farmers, workers, law enforcement, and faith leaders all agree that it is past time for comprehensive immigration reform.

To spur job growth and drive our economy forward, we must pass comprehensive immigration reform. I helped introduce legislation during my first term that would create an earned path to citizenship for those who are here, working, and with no criminal record. It would make our nation safer, while also eliminating backlogs, reuniting families, and would meet the demands of our nation’s economy today and into tomorrow. I will continue to keep fighting for comprehensive immigration reform.

I’ve voted against hyperpartisan bills that write a blank check for ICE without meaningful reforms because the agency under Trump has stoked fear and escalated tensions in our communities. We need legal guardrails to prevent ICE from committing violence and terrorizing our communities.

I was horrified by Renee Good’s and Alex Pretti’s killings. Their tragic deaths are part of an alarming pattern of excessive force being used by ICE officers against American civilians without any regard for accountability.

That is why I am pushing for common-sense reforms that require law enforcement officers and agents of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to display identification when detaining or arresting individuals, require judicial warrants, ensure investigations into all DHS-related shootings are independent and transparent, require that federal agents are properly trained, and held accountable for their actions and more.
I am also a cosponsor of the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, to codify protections for immigrants in sensitive locations such churches, hospitals and schools.

pages.title: Pramila for Congress
paragraphs: Standing up to Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the entire extreme MAGA agenda takes ALL of us working together.
Join our movement today and learn how you can make a difference!

pages.title: About Pramila — Pramila for Congress
paragraphs: Elected Experience: United States Representative, 2017-current; Washington State Senator, 2015-2017
Other Professional Experience: Founder/Executive Director, OneAmerica; Director, PATH Fund for Technology Transfer; Financial Analyst; Author
Education: BA in English & Economics, Georgetown University; MBA, Northwestern University

Community Service: Chair Emerita, Congressional Progressive Caucus; National Health Policy Chair, Bernie Sanders Presidential Campaign; Health Care Co-Chair, Biden-Sanders Unity Task Force; Vice Chair, Congressional LGBT Equality Caucus; Co-Chair, United for Climate and Environmental Justice Task Force; Co-Chair, Women’s Working Group on Immigration Reform; Immigration Chair, Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus; Member, City of Seattle Income Inequality Advisory Committee – enacting path to $15 minimum wage

Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal represents Washington's 7th Congressional District, which encompasses most of Seattle and its surrounding areas. She is the first and only South Asian American woman ever elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and one of just two dozen naturalized citizens currently in Congress.

Rep. Jayapal is the Chair Emerita of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, having led the Caucus for six years, growing it into a powerful voting bloc and establishing term limits. She serves on key committees, including the Steering and Policy Committee, the House Budget Committee, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Judiciary Committee, where she is the first immigrant to ever serve as Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration.

In Congress, Representative Jayapal has been a leader on a wide range of landmark progressive issues. She introduced the Medicare for All Act to guarantee health care as a human right, the Housing is a Human Right Act to invest billions into affordable housing, and the College for All Act to make public colleges and universities free for families making up to $125,000 while making community college and trade schools free for everyone. She also introduced the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act to ensure the ultra-rich finally pay their fair share, the Roadmap to Freedom Immigration Resolution to humanely reform America’s broken immigration system, the Dignity for Detained Immigrants Act to stop the use of private, for-profit detention centers, the Access to Counsel Act, and the Ending Platform Monopolies Act to rein in Big Tech’s monopolistic practices while supporting small businesses, consumers, and workers.

Additionally, Congresswoman Jayapal has long been a champion for a $15 minimum wage, racial justice, the PRO Act to support workers’ rights, reproductive justice, the Domestic Workers Bill of Rights, and climate action so we finally transition to a 100% clean energy economy while prioritizing environmental justice and ensuring everyone has access to clean air, safe drinking water, and public lands.

She has spent over 20 years leading organizing and advocacy efforts for women's and immigrant rights and racial and economic justice. She spent 12 years as the founder and Executive Director of OneAmerica, the largest immigration advocacy organization in Washington State. Prior to that leadership, she spent almost a decade working on global health and development for the Program for Appropriate Technology in Health (PATH), an international nonprofit organization.

Born in India, Representative Jayapal grew up in India, Indonesia, and Singapore before coming to the United States by herself at the age of 16. She attended college at Georgetown University and later received her MBA from Northwestern University before working in a number of industries in both the public and private sector. She is the author of two books, Pilgrimage to India: A Woman Revisits Her Homeland and Use the Power You Have: A Brown Woman’s Guide to Politics and Political Change.
She lives in West Seattle with her husband Steve Williamson, a long-time labor leader, and their dog Otis! She is also the proud mother of a daughter and stepson.

pages.title: Home - Nirav Sheth
paragraphs: I firmly believe that our fight should not be against each other but for each other.

I was born and raised in India and came to the US in 2008 as a student of computer and electrical engineering where English became my fourth language. I joined the Marines and proudly served four years as an aircraft mechanic and military police officer. I then continued to serve the people as a police officer here in Lakewood, WA in 2017.

I found my home here in the United States and worked my way from being homeless into becoming a successful business owner in Pierce County. My passion has been to help others come out of similar poverty situations and improve the lives of all those around me. My goal running for office is to unite us by enabling each of us to achieve our dreams by creating safe communities, strong infrastructure, and a bright future for our next generation.

Supporting our emergency services and making crime illegal again in Washington State is crucial. By providing adequate funding and better equipment, we can ensure the safety of our communities and enable law enforcement and fire departments to respond effectively to emergencies.

Collaborating with parents, educators, and local communities is key to creating an education system that prioritizes critical thinking skills and independent thought. Together, we can ensure a brighter future for our students.

Infrastructure is a critical foundation for a thriving economy. By investing in stronger and safer transportation systems, ensuring the resilience of our electric grid, and providing support for small businesses, we can create a conducive environment for economic growth.

As an Immigrant, I know that legal immigration not only ensures a successful integration into our great nation but also upholds the values of fairness, opportunity, and diversity that make the U.S. a beacon of hope for those seeking a better life.
Unite with other volunteers to help Sheth bring his message to all of the 7th District.

pages.title: Affordability Economy Employment - Nirav Sheth
paragraphs: Washington’s Working Families Deserve a Break

Olympia’s spending spree has created a tax tsunami that’s crushing working families and small businesses. Democrats are not fixing our affordability crisis because they are causing it. Layers of taxes are driving up the cost of everything from rent to groceries.

While claiming their state income-tax scheme will put money “in the pockets of Washingtonians,” we’ve already seen Democrats float a lower threshold — as low as $135,000 — which will affect our voters, living in expensive King County, the most.
• 3rd-highest gas tax in the nation — going up to 56.5¢ per gallon starting this summer.
• Climate Commitment Act: a hidden tax currently adding an additional 56¢ per gallon and inflating grocery and utility costs.
• New in 2025 “ sales tax on services ” on online ads, web services, and live events — another blow to small business.
• Death tax kicking in at $3 million, with the top rate tied for the highest in the nation. Driving the middle class and successful out of our state or face the loss of family legacy.
• Property taxes keep climbing , with Democrats seeking to remove the 1% cap protecting homeowners — forcing seniors out of their homes unfairly.
• Adding the “millionaires tax” with the claim of fixing our “regressive” tax code while refusing to lower the most regressive tax — our sales tax.

Washington was once one of the nation’s fastest-growing economies. Today, rising taxes and heavy-handed regulations are pushing employers and investors away . A capital-gains tax, last year’s record-high estate-tax rate, and a new income tax — now the fifth-highest in the country — have already driven leaders like Jeff Bezos and Howard Schultz to relocate, while companies such as Amazon and Starbucks are shifting jobs out of state.

The results speak for themselves. Washington has fallen from 6th best to 6th worst in tax competitiveness, ranks 48th in cost of doing business, and holds the lowest five-year small-business survival rate in the nation — 41.1% compared with the national average of 51.6%.
It’s a clear message: our policies are chasing out opportunity and crippling the small-business engine that fuels local jobs and growth.
Our plan respects workers, rewards effort, and builds the future:
• Every year Republican legislators present a balanced budget without cutting essential services or raising job-killing taxes. Democrats ignore it.
• Work with federal programs to bring funding and encourage investment in Washington State.
• Restore a business environment that supports technology including AI innovation, keeping our marketplace competitive and stimulating job growth.
• Subsidize trade-school and apprenticeship training for graduates and displaced tech and other workers.
• Audit Climate Commitment tax to measure its impact on consumer prices and ensure funds achieve meaningful results.
• Fix senior property-tax relief by raising qualifying income and simplifying access.
• Investigate fraud, waste, and abuse in government spending.
“Let’s make Washington affordable again — for workers, small businesses, and families.”

pages.title: Immigration - Nirav Sheth
paragraphs: I am running for the 7th Congressional District in Washington State and present a nuanced approach to immigration and border security. As an immigrant myself, I deeply value the contributions of those who come to America seeking opportunities.
I will advocate for a balanced policy that upholds the nation’s sovereignty and ensures safety by securing the borders, while also recognizing the essential role of immigrants in the U.S. workforce.
I will propose reforms to streamline the immigration process, making it more accessible for individuals who wish to work and contribute positively to American society.

My stance is rooted in a love for my adopted country and a commitment to safeguarding its security, ensuring that immigration is managed in a way that benefits both the nation and those seeking a new life in the U.S

pages.title: Public Safety - Nirav Sheth
paragraphs: Since the 2020 “defund the police” movement, public officials have shown dangerous hesitation in enforcing the law . Citizens feel abandoned as serious crimes go unanswered and communities lose trust that anyone is in charge. Washington doesn’t need experimental policing — it needs leaders who enforce existing laws.

The fix is simple: reaffirm rule of law and prioritize law-abiding citizens over criminals . In 2024, conservatives stepped in where politicians failed, passing Initiative 2113 to restore “reasonable suspicion” for police pursuit. That single act reversed the failed 2021 restrictions that handcuffed officers and triggered record car thefts statewide. Our tax dollars pay for public safety — we deserve to feel safe and enjoy our city.

We strengthen safety by backing good officers , removing bad ones when necessary, and rebuilding respect for law enforcement at every level. That includes coordination with federal efforts to remove violent illegal offenders from our communities.
Democrats “reimagined” policing. Republicans restored it.
Their laws produced rising crime and fleeing officers. Our initiatives produce consequences for crime and confidence for communities.

Democrats passed the “anti-sheriff” bill (SB 5974) allowing elected sheriffs to be de-certified by unelected bureaucrats on a commission controlled by the governor — a violation of separation of powers.
They have softened sentencing for convicted felons including sex offenders.
• Support funding from HB 2015 to hire more police ; ensure dollars go to recruitment, training, and retention — not consultants.
• Keep county sheriffs elected, not appointed; voters must choose their law enforcers.
• Restore city rights to accept or refuse state-funded supportive housing linked to drug activity or repeat crime.
• Dedicate cannabis and opioid settlement revenue to local law enforcement and treatment, ensuring communities that need it the most get the help they need.
• Reform the Blake drug-possession “fix” with mandatory treatment for repeat offenders rather than endless dismissals.
“Public safety isn’t partisan — it’s government’s first duty. Restore law, restore safety, restore trust.”

pages.title: Growth & Support For Small Businesses - Nirav Sheth
paragraphs: As a small business owner myself, I possess a firsthand understanding of the challenges and opportunities faced by small enterprises.

I will passionately advocate for nurturing the growth and success of small businesses across the nation. I firmly believe in the necessity of creating a supportive environment where these businesses can thrive. This includes a commitment to reducing the weight of unnecessary government regulations, which often disproportionately impact smaller companies, stifling their growth and innovation. I have a vision where future small businesses are seen not just as the backbone of the American economy, but as vital contributors to the community and national prosperity.

My approach involves a dual strategy: encouraging direct investment into small businesses and streamlining bureaucratic processes to foster a more business-friendly climate. I believe this will unleash the potential of small businesses, driving economic growth and job creation.

pages.title: Strong Infrastructure - Nirav Sheth
paragraphs: I place a strong emphasis on revitalizing America’s infrastructure, recognizing the critical need to upgrade our energy grid, which currently stands vulnerable to potential attacks by hostile foreign entities and is ill-equipped for the demands of a sustainable, energy-efficient future.

I argue that modernizing the grid is essential not only for national security but also for economic progress. Alongside this, I firmly advocate for the maintenance and improvement of our nation’s bridges and roads, understanding that a robust and reliable infrastructure is the backbone of economic growth and efficiency. Investing in these areas is not just about enhancing physical assets; it’s a strategic move to invigorate the economy and create numerous job opportunities for the American workforce.
My vision encompasses an infrastructure that is safe, efficient, and capable of supporting the country’s advancement into a future of renewable energy and economic prosperity.

pages.title: Kim Schrier | Democrat for Congress in Washington's 8th District
paragraphs: Our country is in a pivotal and worrisome moment right now that requires an effective voice and fighter for the people of Washington’s 8th Congressional District. In Congress, I have worked with both parties to deliver real results that matter. And when recent actions by the Trump administration have harmed our community, I have stood up to Trump, his D.C. allies, and his billionaire friends to protect my constituents. We need to address skyrocketing costs. I am taking on big business monopolies when they pad their profits by raising costs for you. When grocery store monopolies jacked up prices, I went after the merger of Kroger & Albertsons; and I led the bill to protect your kids' data from Big Tech. When Trump cut essential Federal agencies, like firing over 30% of the Forest Service, I fought to get those jobs restored so we can have critical wildland fire fighters defending our communities, and rangers protecting our public lands. I’ve worked to protect access to and bring down the cost of lifesaving healthcare, like guaranteeing $35 insulin & lowering prescription drug costs. But so much more needs to be done to reform our healthcare system, starting with undoing disastrous Republican cuts to Medicaid (Apple Health), and restoring the tax credits Republicans cut that helped you afford the cost of your premiums. Undoing the bad stuff isn’t enough though. We need to make sure that doctors and patients make healthcare decisions, not insurance companies or the government. I’ve brought over $57 million dollars back to the 8th District in community projects ranging from school based health clinics to wastewater treatment plants, and returned over $30 million in earned VA benefits, social security payments, and tax refunds. I’ve held over 130 town halls & traveled thousands of miles around this district to meet with you every year. Right now, with a seeming epidemic of self-enrichment and corruption in Washington, D.C., we need accountability, and not just for the president. You deserve a government you trust to work to protect your interests. And you deserve a representative who will always listen to you & deliver. I am so proud to fight for our district, and want to keep delivering for you in Congress.”

pages.title: About Kim | Kim Schrier
paragraphs: I am honored to represent Washington’s 8th Congressional District, and am running for re-election to represent the district which includes much of King, Pierce, Snohomish, Kittitas, and Chelan Counties, and portions of Douglas County.

I am a pediatrician, a wife, and a mom with deep roots in this community. Prior to being elected to Congress, I spent 17 years as a pediatrician listening to and helping solve problems with thousands of patients and their families across the 8th District, and I am bringing that same dedication and understanding to my work as your representative in Congress.

When I first ran for Congress, I promised to be an independent and effective voice for the people of Washington’s 8th Congressional District – someone eager to work with both parties to deliver real results that matter. And that’s exactly what I’ve done. I’m proud to have passed 22 bills into law, signed by both Democratic and Republican presidents.

Our country is in a pivotal moment right now that requires an effective voice and fighter for the people of Washington’s 8th Congressional District. While I’ll always work with anyone on policies that help you, I will also always stand up to anyone who makes life harder for you. The Trump Administration has demonstrated that they are only concerned with increasing the President’s own personal wealth and power along with that of his billionaire friends.

I never planned to run for office, but I knew that I had to join the fight because politicians in Washington were dismantling the healthcare system that, as a person with Type 1 Diabetes, had kept me & people like me alive. Now the fight has grown even bigger as this corrupt administration is not only kicking tens of millions of people off their health insurance, now they’re selling off pieces of the government to the highest corporate bidder. With your support, I will continue the fight to restore our government to one that puts you first.

Even now, when Congress seems hopelessly broken, we’ve notched out some wins – passing a law to streamline building more affordable housing, cutting red tape in the buildout of clean energy, seeking justice for the victims of Jeffrey Epstein and other powerful men, and passing a farm bill that helps 8th District farmers. We’ve passed my Kids Online Safety Act through the House, and I’m hopeful we will get that over the finish line this year. It is long past time to protect our children from Big Tech abuses. With your support, we’ll hold this seat and change the balance of power in Congress. That is how we can restore checks and balances, slam the brakes on this president’s abuse of power, demand accountability, start the process of repairing our nation, and get back to the business of serving you.

pages.title: Meline for Congress | District 08 - Washington State
paragraphs: Together, we can keep the American Dream within reach for working families.

I believe the American Dream is still alive, but it’s getting harder to reach. America is built on innovation, forward-thinking leadership, and the dignity of hard work. That dream has always defined our country. I’m running for Congress to ensure the next generation has the same chance to build a meaningful life.
Wildfire Defense, Forest Health & Natural Resources
Spencer Meline is a small business owner, husband, and father of four who was born and raised in Washington.

He built his businesses from the ground up, gaining firsthand experience managing payroll, navigating regulations, and leading teams through growth and uncertainty. That experience shaped his understanding of how federal policy affects real employers, workers, and families.

Spencer supports parental rights with parents playing a meaningful role in education. He believes there are many paths to success in education—responsibility, discipline, and hard work are essential. Faith is central to Spencer and his family and guides how they live, work, and serve their community.

Spencer has spent years hiking trails, climbing peaks, and fishing remote lakes throughout the wilderness of Washington’s 8th District. Those experiences shaped his deep appreciation for the land and his commitment to responsible stewardship of the public lands that make this region unique.
Spencer is not a career politician—he is a citizen who believes the next generation should inherit the same opportunities and freedoms that built this country.

pages.title: Vision & Priorities | Meline for Congress | District 08 - Washington State
paragraphs: I believe the American Dream is still alive, but it’s getting harder to reach. America is built on innovation, forward-thinking leadership, and the dignity of hard work. That dream has always defined our country. I’m running for Congress to keep that dream within reach for working families and ensure the next generation has the same chance to build a meaningful life.
Washington has become too complicated, too expensive, and too disconnected from the people it serves. Congress should be accountable to the public again.
I support term limits for Congress. Public service should be a season of life, not a lifetime career.
Congress should vote on one issue at a time. No more hiding controversial provisions inside thousand-page bills that members barely have time to read.
Federal spending should be easily searchable and understandable. Americans should be able to see where their money goes without needing an accounting degree to figure it out.

Members of Congress should not be trading individual stocks while making laws that can affect those investments. Retirement accounts, diversified funds, and broad-market investments are one thing; individual stock picking while serving in Congress is another.
Congress needs enforceable restraints on deficit growth and a serious commitment to reducing waste, duplication, and unnecessary federal spending.
Small businesses create jobs, build communities, and provide opportunity, yet federal policy too often works better for the largest corporations than for the entrepreneur trying to get started.

Simplify SBA lending, shorten approval times, reduce unnecessary paperwork, expand access to capital, and strengthen microloan programs so entrepreneurs outside major financial centers have a real opportunity to build something.
Create tax incentives that reward small businesses for investing, hiring, and growing here in America.
Families and small businesses should not need teams of accountants to understand what they owe. Reduce unnecessary complexity and eliminate special-interest loopholes.
Use a competitive tax and regulatory environment to encourage companies to manufacture, invest, and hire in the United States.
Give Struggling Small Businesses Breathing Room

Explore reforms allowing qualifying small businesses experiencing significant revenue declines greater flexibility with quarterly estimated tax payments without being punished for circumstances outside their control.
For too many working families, homeownership is moving further out of reach. We need to increase supply while helping ordinary Americans, not massive institutions, compete for homes.

Encourage housing construction by reducing unnecessary regulatory barriers and using federal infrastructure and housing programs in ways that increase supply while respecting state and local authority over land use.
Provide targeted tax relief that helps working Americans overcome the enormous upfront cost of purchasing their first home.

Modernize capital-gains rules so older Americans who have spent decades building equity aren’t unnecessarily discouraged from selling a larger home and downsizing. Freeing those homes also increases inventory for younger families.
Address large institutional investors accumulating substantial portfolios of single-family starter homes so families aren’t forced to compete against enormous pools of institutional capital.

Test whether qualified homeowners, beginning with an appropriate pilot such as VA borrowers, could transfer an existing mortgage rate when moving to another home rather than becoming trapped by dramatically higher rates.
In Washington’s 8th District, wildfire isn’t an abstract environmental debate. It threatens homes, businesses, forests, recreation, agriculture, and entire communities.
Expand responsible thinning, prescribed burning, hazardous-fuel removal, and other active forest-management practices.
Shift more resources toward year-round prevention and mitigation rather than spending enormous sums only after fires become emergencies.
Maintain strategic forest roads and access routes that firefighters need while restoring responsible access to trails, campgrounds, and recreation.
Washington’s hydroelectric system provides reliable electricity and is an important part of the region’s economy. Protect existing generation while modernizing the electrical grid.

America should pursue abundant, reliable energy, including hydropower, nuclear power, renewables, natural gas, and domestic oil production, to strengthen energy security and keep utility and transportation costs manageable.
Invest in water storage and infrastructure and pursue agricultural policies that recognize the realities facing farmers, growers, and rural communities.

Healthcare has become dominated by enormous systems of hospitals, insurers, pharmacy benefit managers, and other intermediaries. Reform should put patients, families, and local providers back at the center.
Patients should be able to know the actual price of non-emergency healthcare before receiving it, including their expected out-of-pocket cost whenever practicable.
Encourage competition among insurers and healthcare providers and examine interstate insurance reforms that could give consumers more choices while maintaining appropriate protections.
Make it easier for independent physicians and local practices to compete with massive healthcare systems instead of allowing continued consolidation to eliminate community-based care.
Patients should receive clear information about coverage, deductibles, denials, and actual costs.
Give patients and health plans greater flexibility to invest in evidence-based preventive care, nutrition, metabolic health, and other approaches aimed at reducing chronic disease.
There should be more than one path to a successful American life. College is right for some students. The trades, apprenticeships, entrepreneurship, and technical careers are right for others.
Expand access to apprenticeships, technical education, and career training, and stop treating a four-year university degree as the only respectable path to success.

Encourage education in financial literacy, taxes, contracts, budgeting, nutrition, and other practical skills students will actually use as adults, while respecting state and local control of curriculum.

Parents should have meaningful access to information about what their children are being taught and what is happening in their schools, consistent with applicable law and legitimate student protections.

Artificial intelligence may be one of the most consequential technologies of our generation. Government shouldn’t try to stop innovation, but neither should America enter this transition without safeguards for workers, competition, privacy, and national security.
Establish strong federal privacy protections giving individuals greater transparency and control over how their personal information is collected, stored, sold, and used.
Modernize workforce-development and retraining programs so workers displaced or substantially affected by automation have opportunities to move into growing industries.
Enforce existing antitrust laws when dominant technology companies unlawfully suppress competition, while ensuring regulations don’t create barriers that prevent startups from challenging incumbents.

High-impact uses of AI should not become an excuse for institutions to avoid human responsibility. Americans deserve transparency and meaningful avenues to challenge consequential automated decisions.
America should remain the world leader in AI and emerging technologies while addressing national-security risks, critical infrastructure, energy requirements, and foreign adversaries.

pages.title: Home - Adam Smith for Congress
paragraphs: “ I'm fighting to rebuild our representative democracy that Trump has tried to tear down, restore accountability, and lower the cost of everyday life by making sure our government delivers real results for working people. ”

pages.title: Priorities - Adam Smith for Congress
paragraphs: Listen to communities and constituents, set ambitious but realistic goals and expectations, and deliver practical solutions that make life better for everyone in work for people in Washington’s Ninth District.

Adam is relentlessly focused on cutting the cost of housing to lower our rent and keep families housed. In Congress, he has sponsored legislation to make it easier to build affordable housing, especially near transit centers. By slashing construction costs, reducing burdensome red tape, and bringing together local, state, and federal partners, Adam is getting housing built faster and cheaper to address the affordability crisis head on. Adam is cracking down on Wall Street hedge funds that distort our housing market and drive up rents—introducing bicameral legislation to divest private equity from single family homes and allow Americans to build wealth through homeownership.
“Housing is the most important issue to my district in Washington and I’m thrilled to introduce legislation that will tackle this issue in a concrete way”
Adam wrote the End Hedge Fund Control of American Homes Act, forcing corporate landlords to divest single-family homes and leveling the playing field for first-time buyers.

Adam has cut red tape to allow Sound Transit to develop housing near light rail stations via his Promoting Affordable Housing Near Transit Act which has extinguished federal interest in transit agency owner property that is used to build affordable housing leading to over 3,000 affordable housing units being built in King County.
He sponsored a major zoning and permitting reform bill to incentivize cities and counties to cut red tape and build more housing near jobs and transit.
He funded on-the-ground housing solutions through Community Project Funding, securing millions of federal dollars for supportive and affordable housing in Seattle, Bellevue and South King County.
He backed the FHA First-Time Homebuyer Counseling Discount Act, which reduces mortgage insurance costs for new buyers who complete housing-counseling programs.

Donald Trump’s chaos is costing us more every day. Adam is fighting Donald Trump and Republican corruption to restore accountability and protect SNAP benefits for our veterans and seniors, healthcare subsidies for millions of Americans, and Washington’s nation-leading vote-by-mail system. Adam has never backed down from Donald Trump or MAGA extremists who threaten our democracy. Adam has stood up to Trump’s reckless policies at home and abroad, overriding President Trump’s veto to defend democracy and American values, and voting against his dangerous agenda. He will fight tooth and nail to protect our vote by mail system.
“I don’t care who’s in power—if they’re undermining democracy or hurting people, I’ll stand up to them.”

Adam will lead rigorous oversight of the Department of Defense as Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee. Adam has already brokered a bipartisan and bicameral investigation to provide rigorous oversight into the Department of Defense’s military operations in the Caribbean.
Adam cosponsored multiple War Powers Resolutions directing the President to remove United States Armed Forces from Venezuela.
Adam cosponsored the VISIBLE Act, which requires immigration enforcement officers to clearly display visible identification during public-facing enforcement actions

Adam signed onto an amicus brief that continues to affirm Congress’s Article I exclusive legislative power to impose tariffs and regulate commerce and support a lawsuit brought by 12 States’ Attorneys against the Trump Administration for abusing emergency powers under IEEPA to unlawfully impose reckless, across-the-board tariffs.

Adam has been endorsed by leaders across Washington for consistently voting 100% against Donald Trump’s agenda, defending vote-by-mail from GOP attacks, and blocking MAGA proposals to slash SNAP, ACA subsidies, and veterans’ benefits.
Adam led a bipartisan effort to override Trump’s veto, stopping the former president’s attempts to weaken democratic institutions and international alliances.
He is a co-sponsor of the Ensuring Women’s Right to Reproductive Freedom Act, pushing back on MAGA-backed attempts to criminalize interstate travel for abortion.
He co-sponsored the Hands Off Medicaid and SNAP Act to block GOP efforts to slash health care and food assistance for seniors, veterans, and working families.
He supported the State-Based Universal Health Care Act, which protects Washington’s health-care model from attempts to dismantle ACA coverage.

Adam is taking on powerful special interests to create better opportunities for everyone. He supports banning members of Congress from trading stocks, forcing polluters to pay for environmental cleanup, creating a universal healthcare system and he has passed legislation stopping Big Pharma from price gouging life saving medication like insulin. Adam is leading the fight by introducing bills that would stop private equity from monopolizing housing, end the practice of corporations spending billions of dollars on stock buybacks, create a minimum tax rate on massive corporations so they finally pay their fair share, and strengthen financial regulations and oversight on big banks.
“Too many families are struggling to afford to rent or to buy a home… Large investors are buying up homes and squeezing out prospective buyers.’

Adam introduced the End Hedge Fund Control of American Homes Act , a bicameral bill that forces private-equity firms to divest their single-family home portfolios and bans future bulk purchases that drive up rents across Washington.
Adam co-sponsors the Wall Street Tax Act, which taxes high-volume financial transactions to curb speculation and fund public investments.
He co-sponsors the Supreme Court Ethics and Transparency Act, pushing for judicial ethics rules and cracking down on undisclosed gifts to Justices.
He supports the Restore Trust in Congress Act to ban stock trading by Members of Congress to rebuild trust in America’s democratic institutions.
He supports the Fracturing Responsibility and Awareness of Chemicals Act, which requires oil and gas companies to disclose the toxic chemicals used in fracking.
Expand Economic Opportunity & Build Pathways to High Paying Jobs

Adam understands that no one should have to work two jobs just to afford rent and essentials. Fighting for a living wage that you can raise a family and buy a house on is personal to him and that’s why he supports raising the federal minimum wage to $20/hour. Adam’s dad was a rap serviceman at Sea-Tac Airport, and a proud member of the Machinist Union. He understands that the path to good paying jobs and an economy that works for everyone is built by unions and that’s why he’s fighting for more apprenticeship programs and stronger labor protections that ensure our right to bargain and organize. The ability to earn a living wage to raise a family and buy a house should be possible for everyone. Adam’s dad was a ramp serviceman at Sea-Tac Airport, he knows there’s honor in all work and has championed apprenticeships, short-term credentials, and community college pathways.
“A good job should be within reach for everyone who’s willing to work for it.”

Adam co-sponsored the Raise the Wage Act to move the federal minimum wage toward $20/hour and fought to protect collective-bargaining rights as a co-sponsor of the PRO Act, because real economic mobility is built by workers having power.

Adam introduced the Community and Technical College Investment Act and the Career and Technical Education Access Act, two bills designed to expand opportunities for students to access affordable higher education, gain in-demand skills, and build stronger pathways into the workforce.
Adam introduced the Empowering Individuals Through Education and Workforce Training Act, expanding short-term credentials that lead directly to good-paying jobs.
He introduced the Pre-Apprenticeship Wrap-Around Services Act, covering childcare, transportation, and basic essentials so workers can actually complete training.
He co-sponsors the Child Care for Working Families Act, reducing child-care costs and expanding access to early learning so parents can stay in the workforce.
He co-sponsors the FAMILY Act, establishing national paid family leave so workers don’t have to choose between a paycheck and caregiving.

Adam is a passionate steward for our lands, waters, and natural resources. He is fighting the Trump Administration’s efforts to allow Big Oil to drill off Washington’s coast and stopping cuts to wildfire prevention and response. In Congress, Adam secured historic investment in clean-energy jobs and critical green infrastructure, permanent protections for North SeaTac Park, money for regional trails, and essential support for Puget Sound Recovery and Salmon Restoration. He is leading the effort to transition our economy to a clean-energy future by reducing our dependence on foreign energy, creating green jobs and taking on Big Polluters.
“Protecting our environment isn’t just policy—it’s personal. This is our home.”

Adam secured permanent protections for North SeaTac park and final passage of the Protecting Airport Communities from Particle Emissions Act, which requires a study on ultrafine particles, via the FY 24 FAA reauthorization.

Adam secured $80 million in federal funding for King County Metro’s RapidRide I Line expansion project through the Capital Investment Grant Program to upgrade Metro Route 160 and connect residents of Renton, Kent, and Auburn to communities throughout the region.

Adam passed the Sound Insulation Treatment Repair and Replacement Program Act, to help families living near SeaTac Airport and other major airports repair or replace failing sound insulation systems, via the FY26 NDAA.
Adam wrote and re-introduced the Aviation-Impacted Communities Act, steering federal noise and pollution mitigation funds toward neighborhoods under Sea-Tac flight paths.
He authored the Aviation Noise & Emissions Mitigation Act, requiring FAA and EPA action on ultrafine particle pollution around airports.
He supports the West Coast Ocean Protection Act, banning offshore oil drilling along Washington’s coast.
He co-sponsors the Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Reauthorization, protecting critical salmon, shellfish, and Puget Sound habitat.
He supports the CLEANER Act to strengthen environmental cleanup standards and hold polluters accountable for toxic waste.
“Abortion rights are human rights—and I’ll never stop fighting for them.”
Adam co-sponsors the Women’s Health Protection Act to codify Roe nationwide, expand access to contraception, and safeguard IVF.
Adam co-sponsors the Women’s Health Protection Act, restoring Roe and banning medically unnecessary abortion restrictions nationwide.
He co-sponsors the Ensuring Women’s Right to Reproductive Freedom Act, blocking states from criminalizing travel for abortion care (H.R.4099).
He supports the Reproductive Freedom for Veterans Act, ensuring veterans can access abortion services regardless of where they live (H.R.4876).
He co-sponsors the My Body, My Data Act, protecting reproductive-health data from being weaponized by anti-abortion states (H.R.3916).
He backs the EACH Act, which ends the Hyde Amendment and ensures federal insurance coverage for abortion (H.R.4611).

pages.title: Meet Adam - Adam Smith for Congress
paragraphs: Adam Smith was adopted as an infant and raised in SeaTac. His dad was a ramp serviceman at Sea-Tac Airport and was a proud and active member in his Machinists’ Union. The financial stability and benefits offered by union work took care of his family. Adam and his brothers attended Bow Lake Elementary, Chinook Middle School, and Tyee High School.

Adam attended Western Washington University, then transferred to Fordham University earning a degree in Political Science while working nights loading UPS trucks. Soon after, he graduated from the University of Washington School of Law and served as a Seattle City prosecutor, lawyer, and judge pro tempore, focusing on domestic violence and DUI cases.

At 25, Adam ran a door-to-door campaign to unseat a Republican incumbent in his hometown of SeaTac—a race many considered a longshot. He won, becoming the youngest state senator in the nation and later chaired the Law and Justice Committee in Olympia.

After securing re-election to the state Senate despite a national Republican Wave in 1994, Adam ran for Washington’s newly created 9th Congressional District in 1996, defeating the Republican incumbent, Randy Tate, in one of the nation’s most competitive races. Adam has spent his career fighting for South King County and the greater Seattle region.

In Congress, Adam has built a reputation for principled, effective leadership. As the top Democrat on the House Armed Services Committee, he’s fought for service members and veterans, cracked down on wasteful Pentagon spending, and passed bipartisan legislation to build affordable housing. He has invested in mental & behavioral health treatment, pushed for a clean energy future, and to expand economic opportunity for all.
Adam and his wife Sara live in Bellevue. Their daughter Kendall is a UW graduate, and their son Jack graduated from WSU. Adam has coached youth soccer, and Sara has twice served as PTA President.

paragraphs: We must also restore an economy where hard work leads somewhere. People should be able to start a business, buy a home, raise a family, learn a trade, advance in their career, and build a better life. That is the promise of America — and it should not be reserved only for the wealthy, connected, or politically powerful.

Across Washington, families are doing everything right — working hard, raising children, caring for aging parents, serving their communities — yet life keeps getting more expensive and less secure. Housing costs are too high. Groceries are too expensive. Taxes and regulations keep piling up. Too many parents wonder whether their children will have the same opportunities they had.

Safe communities are the foundation of a healthy society. We can show compassion to people in crisis while still holding people accountable for crime, addiction-fueled disorder, and policies that make neighborhoods less safe. Families, seniors, workers, and small businesses all deserve to feel secure.

I’m running for Congress because families deserve a better future. We need to make life affordable again, support parents, strengthen public safety, and rebuild real opportunity for every person to learn, build, and contribute.
I will strive to bring common sense, accountability, and real-world experience to Congress. My focus is simple: affordability, family, safety, opportunity, and a better future for our children.
I respectfully ask for your vote/your donation/your support!

pages.title: About - Doug Basler
paragraphs: Former King County Republican Party Vice Chairman; former Eastside Republican Club President and current Vice President; longtime Republican Precinct Committee Officer; candidate for U.S. Congress.
Founder and President of Prologue Digital Inc., a Washington advertising and video production company; media and marketing professional since 1990; longtime sales trainer and small business owner.
Attended Multnomah University; continuing education through more than three decades of business, media, advertising, sales training, and leadership experience.

Worked with rescue missions, Union Gospel Mission, and the Salvation Army on homelessness outreach; worked closely with at-risk youth; former youth pastor, worship pastor, and longtime church volunteer.
I’m running for Congress because Washington families deserve more than another political revolution. We need an opportunity revolution.

The Seattle area helped build some of the greatest companies in the world — Boeing, Microsoft, Starbucks, Amazon, Costco, and many more. We became known as a place where ideas could grow, workers could prosper, and families could build a better future. But today, big government policies are making it harder to build, hire, afford, and stay. When we become hostile to the very employers and innovators that created opportunity here, we lose jobs, weaken our economy, and make life harder for working families.

Affordability is now a crisis. Families are being squeezed by higher gas prices, energy costs, groceries, housing, insurance, and taxes. The Climate Commitment Act may sound good, but in practice it is driving up the cost of energy while doing little to directly improve the environment. Combined with one of the highest gas taxes in the country, these policies raise transportation, food, and energy costs — and those costs get passed on to families through nearly everything they buy. I believe in family, public safety, faith in God, and faith in each other. We need to love our neighbors again. We have had enough division, anger, and blame. Our problems are real, but we will not solve them by tearing each other apart.

I will be a voice of common sense, moderation, and practical solutions in a highly charged political environment. I believe in safer communities, stronger families, lower costs, responsible government, and an economy where everyone has the opportunity to work, build, serve, and thrive.
I’m Doug Basler, and I would be honored to earn your vote.

pages.title: Issues - Shelley Kloba for State Rep
paragraphs: We live in an era of amazing, quickly emerging technology. Policy must develop along with technology, to protect individuals and workers. As your representative, I have worked for years on consumer data privacy. I started with amending initial bills to add consumer protections, and later, to run bills designed to require privacy by design and grant consumers rights so that they may have more choice and control over where their data is going. Now I am working to create a data broker registry so that companies who are profiting off of the sale of data can be monitored, creating more transparency and accountability to consumers.

I am also addressing some of the potential harms of AI. The People’s Privacy Act, a bill I have sponsored for several years now, includes the right for consumers to opt out of profiling to be used for consequential decisions. These are decisions such as pre-authorization for medical coverage, interviews for job applicants, setting insurance rates, and determining salary and wages, all of which should be determined by people, not AI. While there is a lot of buzz around AI, and lots of investment in it, we must endeavor to understand the limitations of the tool. AI shouldn’t be the only trusted resource when determining important decisions in our lives. I want to ensure that there are guardrails that protect people from potential harms of this evolving technology while allowing it to be used for beneficial purposes. Bottom line, technology should serve people, not exploit them for profit . In the last couple years the Legislature has begun to address this by requiring chatbots to alert users that they are not talking to a human and barring chatbots from having sexually explicit or emotionally-dependent conversations with minors. It is a start towards ensuring AI is used to help Washingtonians, not hurt them.

Data Centers are a hot topic of discussion, and with good reason. While they may bring opportunities for economic development and jobs, these benefits must be weighed against the potential environmental harms and consumer impact. Heat production, noise, water usage, the strain to our already stressed transmission infrastructure and energy generation capacity MUST be considered and minimized. Having spoken at conferences around the country, I am prepared to take everything that I have learned and continue to apply it to Washington. This is a topic that continues to be more and more important, and I look forward to the opportunity to bring my expertise to Olympia.

As a parent and former PTA leader, I envision a public education system that meets the needs of all of our diverse learners. The Legislature has progressed towards this goal by fully funding all-day kindergarten, decreasing class sizes for kindergarten through 3rd grade, and providing increased funding for materials and supplies for classrooms. We have also expanded school breakfast and lunch options to cover every student, making learning easier and supporting every student.

The problem still remains that local school districts pay $3.5 billion out of local levy money for teachers and staff that is supposed to be funded under the basic education allocation to districts. It is critical that we place funding the education system in compliance with the McCleary decision at the top of our agenda. Tax loopholes that do not serve the public interest need to be closed and that funding reallocated to the education system. State revenues need to be ample, sustainable, and capable of earning public support.

We must also give individual districts adequate funding and the flexibility to make spending decisions based on the needs of their student population. This would give districts a way to close the opportunity gap by attracting teachers who are best equipped to meet the needs of the students, in classes that are appropriately sized, with supports to meet their needs and help every student reach their full potential.

Commuters tell me that they spend too much time getting to and from work instead of enjoying time with loved ones. Businesses spend more time than necessary moving goods along our highways. Drivers are concerned over the condition of the roads and bridges. This affects quality of life, economic development, and the safety of the traveling public. I will continue to be an advocate for common sense transportation solutions that help families and workers get where they need to be.

Congestion is a multi-faceted problem with no simple solution. A contributing factor is that there is not enough affordable housing in a reasonable proximity to where people work, creating the “drive till you qualify” phenomenon. More affordable housing and expanded opportunities to telecommute can help reduce the number of commuters on the roads. We also need to add more frequent and reliable bus options, plan for rail, strengthen the incident response system on our highways so that blockages can be cleared up more quickly, and allow hard shoulder running for buses during peak times in places where there are no dedicated high-occupancy-transit lanes.

Access to healthcare should never be tied to your employment status. It is a right, not a privilege. Expenses continue to escalate and it is vital we work on affordability by getting rid of the middleman to bring costs down. We also need to pivot towards preventative care and treatment of chronic conditions. Not only is this better for every individual’s quality of life, but it also helps the state save money, helping create more funding for those who need it.

The consolidation of hospitals and clinics often leads to closure of small rural providers and can be particularly problematic when one of the acquiring entities is religion-based. This results in lack of care for reproductive and end-of-life issues in these areas. We need to work with the full spectrum of healthcare providers to make sure that healthcare is accessible to all Washingtonians, not just those with jobs that live in metropolitan areas.

Behavior healthcare resources are also vital in every community. Too often our law enforcement officers respond to calls involving behavioral health issues that they are not always equipped to handle. One solution we have implemented in the 1st LD is the regional crisis response system, an agreement that makes Crisis Responder Mental Health Professionals available to respond with the police calls that involve a behavioral health crisis. We have also built crisis treatment centers, that people in crisis can access on their own and law enforcement can bring someone to instead of jail or the emergency room. This frees up officers to get back out on patrol after an incident, optimizing their time. This is the start towards human-centered solutions that provide the appropriate kind of care to individuals who need it. As a representative, I am always looking to help foster these kinds of solutions to ensure every community can meet the needs of its members.

I hear constantly from voters that affordability and the economy are top priorities. With high gas prices and increasing costs of everyday items, it is important to look at how the legislature can make life more affordable for individuals. I support a fair taxing system that does not create undue burden on individuals, especially those at the lower half of the earning spectrum, ensuring that everyone pays their fair share.

This past session, the Legislature passed the Millionaires Tax. In addition to taxing every dollar after the first million of net income, the law also created various tax breaks. It nearly doubled the number of families who qualify for the Working Families Tax Credit, cut B&O Taxes for small businesses, removed sales tax on hygiene products and over-the-counter medicines, and created free breakfast and lunch programs for every K-12 public school student in Washington. This, along with the capital gains tax, is the start of correcting our state’s upside down tax code. I will continue to support bills that create fair tax systems.

I am committed to working towards community-oriented solutions to address housing issues and homelessness in our state. In Olympia I worked to secure over 5 million dollars in the budget to work towards creating low-income housing in Kenmore. Although community opposition killed the proposed project, I remain committed to working with stakeholders to find solutions for the lack of low-income housing in our area. In a country as wealthy as ours, it is unconscionable that we have people who sleep outside every night with no place to call home. The issue will not go away without coordinated, sustained effort. To have a healthy community, we must do everything possible to encourage a variety of types, styles, and affordability levels of housing options that serve folks at every income level.

We are fortunate to live in a beautiful region, and I remain committed to protecting and promoting our high quality of life. To me that means ensuring the highest air and water quality, preserving parks and open space, and reducing our dependence on fossil fuels to preserve our environment for future generations.

As Washington reduces greenhouse-gas emissions, invests in renewable energy, and transitions away from a fossil fuel economy, we have a tremendous opportunity to create and maintain a thriving alternative energy industry to drive our state’s economic growth and employ a stable workforce. As a State Representative, I will aim to serve as a leader on environmental issues by supporting programs that make our community more sustainable, including prioritizing statewide funding for waterway monitoring and infrastructure improvements for water supplies, providing incentives for new technologies, developing workforce re-training programs, and strengthening our state’s commitment to green energy sources.

I also stood for smart growth and smart investments that maintain our high quality of life while planning for our region’s future.

In addition, I was actively involved in supporting our kids and families on the Eastside Human Services Forum, the King County Domestic Violence Initiative, the King County Cities Climate Collaboration, and the King County Board of Health. I also served a four-year term on the Kirkland Park Board, volunteered on park and school bond and levy committees, and served as a trustee for the Lake Washington Schools Foundation. Over the past 15 years I have worked to meet the needs of all our residents.

In the Legislature, I have done my best to represent you. Your voice matters to me. I look forward to returning to Olympia to continue to work towards an economy that works for everyone, a high quality school system that meets the diverse needs of every student, environmental policies that conserve our natural resources, and the health and safety of all our residents.
