pages.title: Elect Zach Hall
paragraphs: We’re so blessed to call Washington State home. With its incredible natural beauty, our access to the outdoors is unrivaled. We lead the nation in environmental stewardship and climate action. With a culture of innovation and thriving aerospace, agriculture, tech, and maritime industries, we consistently rank among the strongest and most diverse state economies. We’re committed to equality and opportunity.

We’re on the right track, but we’re not without our challenges. Families are still struggling, still stretching every dollar they earn. Our housing crisis is still as urgent as ever, access to affordable childcare and healthcare is still out of reach for too many, and our schools still need more funding to engage, support, and prepare our students for the future. I’m running to retain my seat to continue fighting for safer, more affordable communities.

Zach was appointed to the Washington State House of Representatives in June 2025. In his first session, he sponsored and passed bipartisan bills to lower energy costs, prioritized safety and congestion improvements along State Route 18, and supported reforms to help fix our housing crisis, modernize our power grid, and build light rail faster.

Before joining the state legislature, he served for six years on the Issaquah City Council, leading efforts to expand funding for affordable housing, public safety, environmental protection, and transportation infrastructure. He also chaired the Eastside Fire & Rescue Board of Directors, ensuring our first responders were equipped with the tools and resources they needed to keep families safe.
I’m honored to have the support of trusted leaders and organizations here in district and across the state.
✔️ Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates

pages.title: Priorities — Elect Zach Hall
paragraphs: Working families are stretching every dollar they earn. It’s never been more important to keep everyday essentials affordable – like groceries, housing, healthcare, and childcare – and protect the essential services our communities rely on.

Our housing crisis is urgent and everywhere. Supply is low, demand is high, and costs are through the roof. We need more affordable housing and reforms that make it easier to finance and build new homes faster.

Our roads and bridges should be properly preserved and maintained. It’s essential to our region’s economy and quality of life, and I’ll continue to prioritize investing in the infrastructure we rely on every day.

Finish State Route 18. Now that the new interchange at I-90 and State Route 18 is open, it’s more important than ever to protect the funding we’ve won to expand this major corridor. I'll also push to implement more immediate safety and congestion improvements now.

We need more choices. It should be quick, safe, and easy to get where you need however you choose. Focusing on transit access and local grants for connected bike networks and pedestrian safety helps us achieve that goal.

Fully fund our schools so every student is engaged, supported, and prepared for the future. I grew up attending Issaquah public schools myself, and I know that investing in our classrooms and educators is the surest way to improve student learning outcomes and set our graduates up for success.

Safe communities need comprehensive supports. That means equipping our first responders with the tools and resources they need, proactively responding to the threat of wildfires and floods, preventing gun violence, and investing in behavioral health and substance use interventions that meet people where they are when they need them.

We lead the nation in environmental stewardship and climate action. I’m committed to protecting public lands and natural resources, investing in salmon recovery and habitat restoration, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions by transitioning to cleaner, more renewable energy resources.

Modernize our energy grid. We need significant investment in transmission infrastructure to meet our growing energy needs. By upgrading and expanding our aging power grid, we can transition away from fossil fuels faster, build capacity for future growth, make our systems more reliable and resilient, and lower energy costs for everyone.

Michelle Bennett is running for State Representative in Washington’s 5th Legislative District to protect working families, defend taxpayers, elevate public safety and bring practical, accountable leadership to Olympia.

Families across the 5th Legislative District are working harder than ever, but Olympia keeps making life more expensive. From higher taxes to rising energy, housing, and everyday costs, too many decisions in state government are being made without enough concern for the people who have to pay the bill. Michelle Bennett believes Washington needs a different approach: protect taxpayers, fund core priorities, support public safety, strengthen schools, and make government more accountable to the people it serves. And Michelle serves everyone in the 5th Legislative District, not a party affiliation. She is running as a Republican to reflect her fiscal values and the needs of the people in the 5th.
Michelle will oppose efforts to expand Washington’s income tax and fight for tax policies that protect working families, seniors, small businesses, and local communities.
State government should set priorities, measure results, and respect taxpayers. Michelle will push for disciplined budgeting and practical solutions.
Michelle supports law enforcement, first responders, local schools, small businesses, and the infrastructure families rely on every day.

The current direction in Olympia is clear: more taxes, more spending, and less accountability. Michelle Bennett believes families in the 5th District deserve a representative who will ask harder questions, protect household budgets, and stand up when state government goes too far.

pages.title: Lisa Callan for State Representative, 5th Legislative District, Position 2
paragraphs: Democrat for State Representative · 5th LD · Position 2
An engineer, a mom, and a budget writer for the 5th LD.
Lisa got into this work the way a lot of parents do. She watched what state budget decisions did to her kids' classrooms, and she decided the cleanest fix was to help write the budget herself.

Before Olympia, Lisa was a lead engineer and project manager at Boeing and a software consultant. She and her husband Bryan raised their son in the Issaquah Highlands, where she served two terms on the Issaquah School Board, including a stint as president.
In 2018, she became the first Democrat in modern memory to win the 5th LD's Position 2. She has won every election since by larger margins. In 2024, she took 56% of the vote.

In Olympia, Lisa serves as Vice Chair of the Capital Budget. In January 2026, she stepped in as Acting Chair and led negotiations on a $910 million supplemental budget that put more money into school construction, affordable housing, and flood response. She co-chairs the state's Children & Youth Behavioral Work Group and serves on the Education and Children, Youth, and Families committees.

The work has results. Five Callan bills passed the House in 2024 alone. Her HB 2180 raised the cap on special education funding and passed both chambers without a single no vote. Her early-learning bills helped lock in roughly $100 million for childcare construction. Her HB 1580 created the Children & Youth Multisystem Care Coordinator to find homes for kids stuck in hospital ERs.
Lisa with her husband Bryan and their son.
Three connected lanes: the Capital Budget, kids and behavioral health, and education. Here is what that has produced.

Raised the cap on special education funding from 15% to 17.25% (HB 2180, passed without a no vote). Helped negotiate $1 billion for K-12 construction in the 2025-27 capital budget, plus $109 million more in the 2026 supplemental for small district and tribal compact schools and seismic upgrades.

Wrote HB 1580 to find homes for kids stuck in hospital ERs in psychiatric crisis. Co-chairs the state's Children & Youth Behavioral Work Group. Passed bills funding a behavioral health consult line for pediatricians and school counselors, and is moving HB 2038 to fund youth mental health through a surcharge on social media platforms.

Locked in roughly $100 million for childcare construction through HB 2195 and HB 1314. Expanded early learning grants to tribal compact schools. Named 2024 House Champion of the Year by the Children's Campaign Fund.
Voted for every major gun safety bill since 2019. Prime sponsor of permit-to-purchase, lost-or-stolen reporting, and bulk firearm purchase limits. Endorsed by the Alliance for Gun Responsibility.

96% lifetime score from the Washington State Labor Council. Voted yes on extending unemployment to striking workers. Supports apprenticeship at 15%+ on public works, prevailing wage, and Project Labor Agreements. Pushing apprenticeship into manufacturing and maintenance trades.

Voted for the Climate Commitment Act. Campaigned to defeat the I-2117 repeal effort. Capital budgets she has shaped include heat pump installations, weatherization, fish-passage culverts, and stormwater infrastructure.

Helped negotiate $776 million for housing and homelessness in the 2025-27 capital budget, plus $150 million more in the 2026 supplemental. Supports ADUs, lot splitting, and density along transit corridors. Focused on suburban East and South King County, where the price-to-income gap is widest.

Prime sponsor of HB 2225, the Governor Request Bill regulating AI companion chatbots: detection of self-harm and suicidal ideation, content filters and disclosures for minors, and a ban on manipulative engagement techniques.
The people who know the work, Stand with Lisa.
“Callan brings the kind of substance the 5th LD deserves in Olympia.”
“Lisa Callan is the legislator Washington kids needed in this seat.”

“As both State Senator for the 5th LD, and as the mother of two young children in our public schools, I have seen firsthand how important it is to have champions for public education representing us in Olympia. Representative Lisa Callan has secured major victories for our communities by raising the cap on special education funding and delivering much-needed investments in school construction and behavioral health for young people. Lisa is a dedicated advocate for working families, and she consistently fights to ensure every child in Washington has the resources and opportunities they need to thrive. It is my honor to endorse her re-election.”

“Since 2018 Lisa has been working tirelessly to fully fund our schools, keep our neighborhoods safe, and invest in our community. She has been a tremendous advocate for our district in Olympia, and I know she will continue fighting for us in the upcoming session, and we are so very lucky to have her represent us!”

pages.title: David Hackney Campaign for Washington's 11th Legislative District
paragraphs: My name is David Hackney, and I am honored to serve as your State Representative

As a former Assistant US Attorney with experience working with the United Nations, the Nature Conservancy, and employment and labor law, David brings an incredible breadth of experience to Washington’s 11th District.

pages.title: Priorities — Hackney for the 11th
paragraphs: The 11th is one of the few affordable areas left in King County, but rising property taxes and housing prices threaten to disrupt our community. For too long, the issue of housing has only been on city and regional radars, and not its impact in rural and small, but nascently influential, communities like those in the 11th. In the legislature, I have guided my fellow lawmakers to take action on housing now in a way that supports smaller areas via clean and green measures, transit-friendly and multifamily builds, and more.

One of my bills that successfully passed created a real estate tax exemption for sales of property designated as affordable housing. Washington needs way more housing than we currently have; therefore, mechanisms for funding and supporting affordable housing needs are necessary. This bill will help the state reach its housing goals.

Here in the 11th we suffer some of the highest levels of environmental health risks in the entire state, particularly with regard to air and noise pollution. We have a responsibility at the state level to ensure we are doing everything we can to combat the climate crisis and keep our communities healthy. I’m proud my bill requiring building owners must ensure their properties meet green energy performance standards passed, and look forward to creating more legislation that make our communities green, healthy, and sustainable, while mitigating the effects of climate change.

The state has set the goal of reducing our carbon emissions in half by 2040. I have become a co-chair of the bipartisan Hydrogen Caucus with Republican Rep. Peter Abbarno of Gig Harbor, and I am excited and confident in our bipartisan approach to enacting green fuel policies as part of our state’s push to reduce carbon pollution.

When I was younger, my family suffered a healthcare crisis that crippled us financially. There are far too many people in the 11th who are dealing with similar healthcare crises and the costs associated with it. The legislature can and should do more to lower the burden of healthcare costs.

The pandemic has also revealed just who fragile our healthcare system is and why need to take immediate action to improve it. We are losing nurses and doctors at an alarming rate which is leaving hospitals understaffed and causing people to have to wait to receive care. That is why I am committed to working on policies that will increase our healthcare workforce and reduce burnout.

The COVID pandemic has shown us lingering inequalities and accessibilities affecting many Washingtonian students. We must take the lessons we learned from the pandemic, such how access to reliable internet can make or break a student’s academic performance, providing reliable resources for alternative learning, and better financial and material support for teachers, if we want to do everything we can to close the opportunity gap, support teachers, and prepare our students for the future.

As an attorney and a former federal prosecutor, I have seen first hand the devastation gun violence causes in our communities. Much of this violence is preventable, and I have pursued common sense legislation like banning high capacity magazines that will keep our families and district safe.

We’re experiencing increased incidents of crime that shake public safety. As a federal prosecutor, I know what works to reduce crime: accessible mental health resources, punishment with a focus on rehabilitation, better resources for jails and prisons, and smart data driven policies that enable law enforcement personnel to do their jobs and ensure that people who do commit crimes will not reoffend.

We can reduce crime without over policing of marginalized communities if we address the root causes of crime, and improve crime response resources. This means investing in peer groups like Choose180 and Community Passageways who help mentor youth away from the criminal justice system and create second chance opportunities for people.
If you have any further questions about where I stand on the issues, please call me at 206.717.4439 or send me an email at david@hackney4the11th.com and I'll get back to you as quickly as I can!

pages.title: About David Hackney — Hackney for the 11th
paragraphs: My name is David Hackney, and I am seeking reelection for State Representative here in the 11th Legislative District because our district deserves a fighter. By all accounts and purposes, I shouldn’t be in this race right now. In fact, my whole life has been shaped by opportunities that arose from difficult circumstances.

My family’s history is this country’s history. My paternal grandfather George, was a Pullman Porter and a member of the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters. (the first African-American union in the United States) As a result of the protection of his economic and civil rights by his union, he made the improbable journey from an impoverished agricultural worker to the Black middle class during the depression. My maternal grandfather John, was a sharecropper. He moved north during World War II as part of the great migration of African-Americans fleeing the Jim Crow south. He later joined the United Automobile Workers union, where he made tanks and later freight trucks for 37 years, without missing a day of scheduled work. I am very proud of the accomplishments of my grandparents.

I was born in Cleveland, Ohio, the youngest of three. My father had a job that required us to move frequently. By the time I entered college, I had attended five different schools in three states. My family stayed just long enough to make friends and join the community, before we packed our bags and moved to the next city.

My background has allowed me to be an effective legislator on the issues that that matter most to our district - public safety, economic opportunity in rural and traditionally disadvantaged neighborhoods, climate protection , human rights , gun safety , and fair justice systems . I would be honored to continue using this experience in Olympia to fight for residents in the 11th District.

Neither of my parents completed college, but they did everything in their power to make sure my siblings and I received a quality education. This meant moving to neighborhoods that they could barely afford to ensure my siblings and I went to good schools. At the time, I didn’t fully appreciate the sacrifices my parents were making and my grades suffered. When I got to high school, my grades were so low that the school assigned me to remedial classes. Fortunately for me, my parents demanded that I take college prep classes. As a result of love and guidance from my parents, I buckled down on my studies, excelled in high school, and received scholarships and financial aid to attend Cornell University.

During my Senior year of college, my family experienced a healthcare crisis. My mother was diagnosed with terminal cancer. Shortly after my mother's diagnosis, my father was temporarily laid off as part of a corporate merger, causing a break in our family’s health insurance. When my father resumed work, the company refused to provide health care benefits for my mother, because she had a "pre-existing condition." My sister dropped out of college to take care of our mother, and the healthcare costs crippled my family financially. I nearly had to drop out as well, but the university President provided me a personal loan so I could complete my senior year. I am proud to say I graduated with 20 job offers and have paid the President back in full.

Several years passed and I went to Harvard Law School, because I realized that I could positively impact people’s lives through the law. While in law school, I also earned my Master’s degree in public administration from the JFK School of Government at Harvard. After graduating, I began my legal career as an Assistant United States Attorney for the U.S. Department of Justice, where I tried more than 20 criminal jury trials including homicide, narcotics, fraud, tax, and bank robbery cases. During my 11 years at the Department of Justice, I also taught trial advocacy at the National Advocacy Center, and at the United Nations Mission in Kosovo. I also took a leave of absence from the Department of Justice to work for the UN in The Hague, Netherlands as a war crimes prosecutor. At the UN, I was a member of a trial team that convicted a detention camp commander of crimes against humanity.

After my time working for the UN and Justice Department, I spent several years working with companies to bring broadband to rural and economically disadvantaged communities. I then had the privilege of serving as the Senior Counsel for Global Human Resources at The Nature Conservancy, the largest Non-Profit organization in the world dedicated to preserving the environment.

The last several years I have had the opportunity to devote myself even further to causes I believe in. In 2018, I joined the Boards of Tabor 100 and the Alliance for Gun Responsibility Foundation , where I advocate in the state of Washington on behalf of civil rights and responsible gun laws, respectively. In 2019, Governor Inslee appointed me as a Commissioner on the Washington Human Rights Commission , and then prior to being elected for the first time in 2020 I served as the Director of Legal Affairs and Human Resources for a start-up non-profit that is attempting to build the largest paid membership organization in the United States, dedicated to addressing income inequality.
My life has been shaped by opportunities, and as your State Representative I will continue to work every day to ensure everyone has access to the same opportunities that will allow them to thrive .
My life has been shaped by opportunities, and as State Representative from the 11th I will continue to work every day to ensure everyone has access to opportunities that will allow them to thrive .

pages.title: Home - Ashley Fedan
paragraphs: “For over two decades, I have dedicated my life to public service and public health– both as a nurse and a Navy veteran. As families are squeezed by rising costs of living, as access to healthcare is denied to our most vulnerable, and as basic human dignity is stripped away by our federal government, we need leaders who are willing to fight with compassion, care, and humility.
I am running for State Representative to bring fight, experience, and compassion to Olympia because caring for the community is more than just words to me—it’s who I am and why I serve.”

Born and raised in West Virginia, Ashley began her career at the Cleveland Clinic as a nurse in the cardiothoracic intensive care unit (ICU) in 1999. She traveled across the country, where she continued working as an ICU nurse until 2007, when she attended graduate school in nurse anesthesiology.

While working as a travel nurse, she specialized in critical care, with a cardiac focus, at several hospitals in the San Francisco and Seattle areas, including the University of Washington Medical Center and Harborview Medical Center.

Dedicated to service, Ashley joined the Navy Nurse Corps in 2012 and served as a Lieutenant Commander in the Navy Reserve. She proudly served in the Nurse Corps, leaving the military with the same rank as her grandfather—following in her family’s footsteps of service to her community and country.

pages.title: Priorities - Ashley Fedan
paragraphs: I’ve spent my career inside healthcare systems that put profits ahead of people. I’ve watched families delay care, skip medications, and skip follow-up visits, simply because they were afraid of the bill.

I believe healthcare is a human right, not a privilege reserved for those who can afford it. Ask anyone, from any political party, where they’d want to go if they were having a heart attack, stroke, or broken leg. Nobody hesitates to seek care in a crisis. We all understand, deep down, that care shouldn’t depend on affordability.

I’ll advocate for transparency and accountability from insurance companies and hospital systems. I’ll fight to make sure our state is training enough nurses and healthcare workers to keep up with demand- I’ve experienced, firsthand, how hard it is for patients to get timely care when the system is stretched too thin. Healthcare should heal people. It shouldn’t bankrupt families.

No family should be one bad month away from losing their home. I’ve seen what that kind of stress does to people. The despair shows up in our community long before it ever shows up on the news. A missed paycheck, a rent increase, an unexpected repair bill, any one of those can be the difference between stability and crisis for a family that’s already stretched thin. Too many people in the 11th District are working full-time, sometimes more than one job, and still can’t find a place they can afford to live. It’s not indicative of personal failures–it’s indicative of a system that isn’t working the way it should. No family should be surviving paycheck to paycheck, breath to breath, on life support.

Cut through bureaucratic delays that slow down affordable housing projects, so good developments are built instead of permits that sit on desks for years. Housing is a basic human need- I will address it as such in the legislature.

Push for stronger partnerships between the state and the nonprofit organizations that have established effective methods for building affordable housing. They shouldn’t have to fight a system to do the work our community desperately needs.
Housing stability is the foundation of how a family’s life is built- I intend to treat it that way in Olympia.

The 11th District is full of nurses, construction workers, warehouse employees, caregivers, and neighbors who work hard every single day. Many feel like they can’t get ahead, no matter how many hours they put in at the workplace. I understand that struggle because I’ve lived alongside it my whole life. I grew up in a coal mining community in West Virginia, where I watched corporations swallow an entire town–they closed down factories, and left families with nothing after generations of hard work. That experience never left me. It’s why I became a nurse, and why I’m running now.

As a nurse, I’ve spent my career fighting for the people in the room who don’t always have a voice, whether that’s a patient who can’t advocate for themselves or a coworker facing unsafe working conditions. I’ll bring that same fight to Olympia. I’ll push for wages that actually keep up with the real cost of living, not just small adjustments that fall further behind every year. I’ll continue to stand behind workers who want fair treatment, safe conditions, and a voice in their working lives. Everyone deserves the basic dignity of a safe work/life balance, where a paycheck equals security, safety, and a place in the community.

paragraphs: Stacy is a banker, nonprofit president, daughter of a veteran, and proud resident of Washington’s 12th Legislative District. She has spent years building community and solving problems. Now she’s running to represent Washington’s 12th in the State House of Representatives.

Stacy is a banker, nonprofit president, daughter of a veteran, and proud resident of Washington’s 12th Legislative District. She has spent years building community and solving problems. Now she’s running to represent Washington’s 12th in the State House of Representatives.
Government should work for everyday people, not special interests or party insiders. That’s what drives Stacy Willoughby.

A Washington native who grew up living all over the world , Stacy has called the mountains above Lake Chelan home for almost a decade, where she lives with her husband, Rick, their two dogs, and seven chickens.

With more than 25 years working in financial services, Stacy has seen firsthand how issues like housing affordability and rising taxes impact everyday people across our communities. She’s running to bring that real-world perspective to Olympia, and to make sure we aren’t an afterthought.

Stacy doesn't just talk about community — she’s built it. She brings years of hands‑on leadership in Chelan County and beyond. Through her volunteer work including serving as the Board President of Chelan Valley Hope, and her role on the Chelan Chamber of Commerce Board, Stacy has earned the trust of her neighbors across the district.

She loves working with families, small business owners, and community partners to tackle the challenges from Wenatchee and Chelan to Monroe and into King and Snohomish Counties. Her goal is to improve lives across rural and mountain communities and the growing suburban areas.

Stacy knows the pace of life is different in the 12th, and her leadership reflects our values: hard work, fiscal responsibility, and common sense. She’s dedicated to bringing our perspective to Olympia and doing what it takes to let our voices be heard.

She supports smart, locally driven economic development that creates good jobs without sacrificing the outdoor heritage and quality of life that make this region special. Stacy will champion workforce training, small business support, and partnerships that give local employers and workers the tools they need to grow and stay rooted here.

Housing should be stable, affordable, and available in every community. Stacy believes a safe place to call home is a foundation for working families, seniors, and first-time buyers. She will fight to increase housing supply, crack down on predatory lending practices, and invest in rural and workforce housing so no one has to choose between paying rent and putting food on the table.

Every child deserves a quality education and a clear path to opportunity, no matter their ZIP code. Reliable roads, safe bridges, and fast broadband aren’t extras — they’re essential. She will fight for smart, long-term investments in transportation and broadband that serve rural and growing communities alike and help every corner of the district stay connected to the modern economy.

pages.title: Priorities - Re-Elect Mike Steele
paragraphs: Mike’s legislative priorities focus on strengthening North Central Washington through practical, forward-thinking policies that support families, workers, students, and small businesses.

His work in Olympia centers on improving education and workforce development, supporting responsible budgeting, reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens on employers, expanding economic opportunity, and investing in transportation infrastructure critical to the long-term success of communities throughout the 12th District.

Mike has spent his career advocating for small businesses and understands firsthand the important role they play in creating jobs, supporting local families, and strengthening communities. He believes state government should be a partner in economic success, not a barrier to it. That means creating a regulatory and tax environment that allows businesses to grow, hire employees, and remain competitive in Washington State.
Mike is also committed to improving access to affordable healthcare while protecting choice and working toward long-term cost containment for both employers and consumers.

As a lifelong resident of the district, Mike is proud to represent the communities that shaped him. He remains committed to listening, collaborating, and delivering meaningful results for the people of the 12th Legislative District.

As a member of the Education Committee, Mike worked to address and help satisfy the McCleary court decision requiring ample funding for education in Washington State. While important progress has been made, there is still more work to do.
Mike believes education funding should create additional opportunities for students while supporting clear, rigorous academic standards that prepare young people for long-term success.

Students and teachers in the 12th District deserve the resources they need to succeed, but it is equally important to ensure every dollar invested delivers meaningful results and reflects the changing landscape of education. Mike supports continued expansion of STEM programs and applauds the many schools throughout the district already leading the way in these areas.

Mike supports creating additional opportunities for youth employment and hands-on training programs that encourage innovative, work-based learning strategies. A strong local economy depends on developing and maintaining a skilled workforce.

He also believes increases to the minimum wage must be approached thoughtfully and collaboratively, with consideration for the impact on small businesses, job creation, cost of living, and long-term economic sustainability throughout Washington State.

As a member of the Education Committee Mike worked tirelessly to address and successfully appease The Mcleary court decision to require ample funding of education in our state. There is still more work to be done! I believe that all education funding should provide students with additional opportunists and develop clear and rigorous academic standards.

Students and teachers in the 12 district should have the resources they need to succeed, but we need to make sure every penny we invest is making a difference and addressing the changing landscape of education. I believe we should continue to expand STEM programs and I admire the schools in our 12th district schools that are already focusing on this area of expansion.
I work for and support increasing funding for the community colleges and career and technical programs in our district accompanied by clear expectations for student success.
I support creating additional opportunities for youth employment and training to encourage innovative work-based leaning strategists. The employers of our district need a skilled workforce.

I believe we have to carefully examine increases to the minimum wage. We need to work with small businesses to ensure we are finding solutions that are not about simply increasing the cost of living at all socio-economic levels, increasing the costs of goods sold and make hing employees in all industries more restrictive and less likely.

Employers throughout the 12th District are creating jobs, expanding opportunities, and strengthening the local economy. A vibrant private sector is essential to building a sustainable and prosperous future for communities across North Central Washington. Small businesses continue to play a critical role in supporting local families, communities, and the state economy.
Mike understands the challenges facing small businesses throughout the district, including healthcare costs, overregulation, taxes, workforce shortages, education, and access to skilled employees.

As a representative in Olympia, Mike advocates for policies that support economic growth, encourage innovation, reduce unnecessary barriers for employers, and create a business environment where small businesses can succeed, create jobs, and continue giving back to the communities they serve.

Healthcare remains one of the fastest-rising costs facing both small and large businesses across Washington State. Many employers continue to struggle with the growing expense and complexity of providing quality healthcare coverage for their employees, while also navigating ongoing changes to federal and state healthcare regulations.

Mike recognizes the critical role healthcare providers and local healthcare systems play throughout the 12th District, not only in caring for residents, but also as major employers and economic drivers within many communities.

Mike continues to work alongside healthcare systems, public hospital districts, providers, and community leaders to ensure they have the resources and support needed to serve patients effectively and remain sustainable for the future. He also supports efforts to improve Washington’s healthcare system by increasing affordability, protecting access to care, and creating practical solutions that benefit both providers and patients.

Tourism and hospitality are major economic drivers throughout the 12th District, supporting local businesses, creating jobs, and strengthening communities across North Central Washington. Mike worked alongside fellow legislators to help secure funding for a new statewide tourism initiative aimed at promoting Washington communities and supporting local economies.

In Chelan County alone, tourism generates hundreds of millions of dollars in economic activity each year and supports thousands of jobs throughout the region. From hotels and restaurants to wineries, outdoor recreation, and small businesses, tourism plays a vital role in the long-term economic success of the district.

Mike believes tourism should continue to be a legislative priority, as it remains one of Washington State’s largest industries, generating billions in economic impact and supporting more than 170,000 jobs statewide. Investing in tourism promotion and infrastructure helps create opportunity for local businesses, strengthen rural economies, and showcase the unique communities that make Washington special.

Mike Steele is a proven, bipartisan leader who puts people over politics and delivers real results for North Central Washington.

pages.title: About Claire – Claire Wilson
paragraphs: For the past eight years, Claire has represented the 30th district, advocating for accessible early education, safe and healthy communities, comprehensive sex ed, accessible transportation, environmental protections, and more. She also serves as an advisory board member on the Washington State Family and Community Trust Organization and as a Senate member to the Department of Children, Youth, and Family (DCYF) Oversight Board.

Prior to her election to the Washington State Senate, Claire spent 25 years working for the Puget Sound Educational Service District (PSESD), specializing in early education and family involvement. Before working for the PSESD, Claire taught pregnant and parenting teens at Mt. Tahoma High School, worked as a nutrition educator, and ran a WIC clinic in rural Montana following graduate school.

Claire also has taken a leadership role advocating for kids and families in Federal Way as the School Board President of the Federal Way Public Schools Board of Education, on the State Advisory Committee for Head Start State Collaboration Office (HSSCO), on the Expanded Learning Opportunities Council (ELOC) representing WSSDA’s 295 School Board’s across the state, and as a board member of Region 2 King County, Washington State School Directors Association (WSSDA), and Building Better Futures (BBF) Partnership of Greater Kent Community.

Claire has extensive volunteer experience in South King County and beyond and currently serves as an advisor to the Washington State Leadership Board and the WA State LGBTQ Commission, and as a member of FUSION Federal Way Advisory Council. She has also served on the Advisory Board of the Washington Family Engagement Trust and in South King County on her local PTA, as a member of Citizens for Federal Way Schools, and as a Board member of The Sidekick Collective.

Claire is a proud lesbian woman and mother of two adult children. She is a Washington State native, grew up in Seattle, and graduated from Roosevelt High School and Washington State University. She received her Master’s Degree from the University of Northern Colorado. Now a long-term resident of the 30th LD, Claire has lived in South King County since 1999.

A Guide to the 30th Legislative District

Washington's 30th Legislative District covers Federal Way, Auburn, Algona, Pacific, and parts of Milton and Des Moines in South King County. The district sends one State Senator and two State Representatives to Olympia to represent roughly 150,000 residents.

A State Senator serves a four-year term and votes on the state budget, taxes, public safety laws, transportation funding, and education policy that directly shapes life across South King County. Senators also confirm gubernatorial appointments and help write the laws that local governments operate under.
Not sure if you live in the 30th LD? You can look up your district and current legislators at app.leg.wa.gov/DistrictFinder .

pages.title: Priorities | Elect Jamila Taylor
paragraphs: In addition to my prior work as a nonprofit director, I am a small business owner and manage a complex household budget. I understand the pressures facing local families, the need to maximize resources, and efficient delivery of services. In Olympia I will fight to ensure every family — regardless of employment status and income — can keep a roof over their head and access critical services.

Throughout my career I’ve addressed challenges within the public safety continuum — from preventing youth violence to advocating for the safety of domestic violence survivors and seniors at risk of exploitation. Excessive policing and incarceration should not be the community solution to a problem that has roots in systemic inequity and a lack of social resources. I’m excited to continue tackling these and other critical issues in the legislature.

I firmly believe that parents and guardians deserve access to affordable and free options for day-care. There are many parents who make difficult decisions to leave the job market simply because the family cannot afford childcare. I want families to have a meaningful choice in the matter. In my district, there is a childcare desert. We simply don’t have enough flexible options for families who work second shift. I believe we are long overdue to transform the whole industry to increase resources needed for the workforce and families.

I share my home with my mother and twin brother, both of whom live with chronic illness. Too many seniors and low-income residents are having to choose between life saving medication or having somewhere to sleep at night. I am fortunate that I am able to help provide for my family, but too many others lack a safety net — thus perpetuating cycles of homelessness and other trauma. We have to do better as a State to care for all people. It’s the compassionate and fiscally logical solution.

pages.title: Meet Jamila | Elect Jamila Taylor
paragraphs: Jamila (pronounced JAH-MEE-LAH) Taylor is a public interest attorney and a long-time community advocate. She grew up in California and Oregon with her parents and two brothers. Her father, Quintard, a history professor, and mother, Carolyn, a Girl Scout office administrator, raised her to value education and serving her community. Jamila joined the Girl Scouts in the first grade and remains a lifetime member while continuing to volunteer in King County.

She has served on several nonprofit boards and devoted thousands of hours to various community service opportunities including leading youth development programs and organizational development committees. Jamila joined her first board of directors in 1993 with the American Red Cross of Lane County (Oregon) while she was in high school.

Outside of her passion for community service, Jamila has spent most of her professional career serving the public good. Following her graduation from high school in Oregon, Jamila attended Virginia State University where she studied Sociology. After working a number of years in the private sector, Jamila earned her law degree at the University of Oregon School of Law. While in law school, she dove into diversity and equity efforts in the legal profession via the Black Law Students Association and served on its Western Region and National Executive Boards. Among her many law school activities, Jamila also began to volunteer for an organization that would eventually become BlackPast.org , a free online resource for African American history. BlackPast.org has reached more than 31 million visitors worldwide since its launch in 2007.

Jamila moved to King County in 2007 to begin her legal career. Deeply impacted by the economic recession in 2008, she was unable to find work as an attorney after she passed the bar exam. In the face of this challenge, Jamila focused on volunteerism and social activism. This led her to an opportunity to provide consulting services on behalf of the Urban League of Metropolitan Seattle (“ULMS”) in November 2008 for the Seattle Youth Violence Prevention Initiative (“SYVPI”). By 2009, she was hired on to be the Central Area Network Coordinator / Director of Street Outreach where she coordinated community interventions and supported hundreds of young individuals experiencing conflicts of family, peers, gangs; court involvement; school suspension or expulsion; homelessness and other risk factors. Jamila continued her efforts as the Central Area Network Coordinator when the program moved from ULMS to Therapeutic Health Services in 2011. To enhance her work with SYVPI, Jamila graduated from Leadership Tomorrow in 2013. There, Jamila connected with private sector, nonprofit, and government leaders to address a broad spectrum of regional challenges in the Puget Sound. This led to an opportunity to serve on the Highline College Foundation Board of Directors.

Like many people, Jamila has experienced financial challenges. In 2012, Jamila suffered a medical emergency causing her to be hospitalized in the ICU for five days. After leaving the hospital, she then faced the mounting medical bills not covered by her health insurance. Squeezed by law school, medical, and consumer debt; she could barely afford the rent in Seattle. Jamila had to move several times over the course of six years. Her struggle to find affordable housing in Seattle moved her between Belltown, Queen Anne, Southeast Seattle, and Renton.

In early 2014, Jamila left THS and SYVPI to launch her own legal practice and nonprofit consulting business, NW Prosper Law. Her clients included everyday people who need help with family law matters and nonprofits seeking guidance on program/organization development and workshop facilitation. Starting her own business afforded Jamila the flexibility to help care for her mother, Carolyn, and twin brother, William, who are both facing severe chronic illnesses. Jamila frequently traveled from the Seattle area to Eugene to help her mother and brother. As their needs grew, Carolyn and William decided to move to King County. Jamila, Carolyn, and William made Federal Way their new home in late 2014.

When Carolyn and William were comfortably settled into their new life in Federal Way, Jamila continued her community endeavors. As part of the 2016 graduate of the Washington Leadership Institute, she and her fellow co-hort members produced voter engagement videos available on www.diversevotes.org . Jamila joined Washington’s largest public interest law firm, Northwest Justice Project, in 2017. As a staff attorney she assisted crime victims and domestic violence survivors with their civil needs. In 2018, Jamila was promoted to Statewide Advocacy Coordinator where she worked to enhance community collaborations, help crime victims access civil legal services, and support crime victim attorneys across Washington state. Her work allows her to partner and collaborate with prosecutors, criminal defense attorneys, community-based organizations, and other advocates seeking to end the cycle of crime victimization. She led the Loren Miller Bar Association’s Judicial Evaluation Committee and was recognized by the organization for her efforts to reinvigorate the committee.

Jamila currently serves as an appointee to the Federal Way Human Services Commission and on the board of the Judicial Institute. Lastly, Jamila is completing her term as as the Vice-President of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc. – Delta Upsilon Omega Graduate Chapter and helps to develop its community service efforts throughout Seattle and King County.

pages.title: Issues | Mysite
paragraphs: As a business owner, I understand how challenging it has become to operate in Washington. Businesses are the backbone of our communities across the 30th Legislative District and all of Washington. Rising B&O taxes, increasing payroll costs, regulatory burdens, and complex compliance requirements make it difficult for many businesses to survive.

Over the past decade, Washington has fallen from being one of the more competitive states for business to near the bottom nationally. Businesses are now failing within their first five years at a rate of 59%, the highest in the country. That means fewer thriving local shops, fewer family-owned businesses, fewer stable jobs in our neighborhoods, and more businesses closing their doors.

We need policies that encourage entrepreneurs, family-owned businesses, small businesses, and community-serving companies to start, grow, and stay in our state. I will support responsible local decisions, reduce unnecessary barriers, and advocate for an environment where these businesses can survive and thrive.

Families across Washington are feeling the strain of constant rising taxes, fuel costs, housing, groceries, utilities, and childcare. Every time families begin to catch up, if they can even catch up, another increase hits their household budget.
When everyday expenses rise faster than wages, families are forced to make difficult choices. That is not sustainable. Families shouldn't have to struggle this hard to simply survive.

As your representative, I will vote no on new taxes that burden working families and small and local businesses. We cannot keep asking households to tighten their belts while government spending continues to expand.
Olympia must stop putting financial pressure on families and businesses because it cannot control its own spending. Government should live within its means, just like the people it serves.

Strong families build strong neighborhoods. Strong small and local businesses build strong communities. Our policies should protect affordability, prioritize public safety, and restore responsible budgeting that puts Washington residents first.

Recent audits highlight serious gaps. The Department of Children, Youth, and Families struggled to track more than $415 million in federal childcare funding distributed to thousands of providers. The Department of Community and Human Services awarded over $1.8 billion in grants in 2023 and 2024, more than double the amount in prior years, increasing the risk of mismanagement across multiple contracts.

Taxpayer dollars must be tracked, measured, and evaluated for results. This requires independent audits with real follow through, transparent reporting the public can easily access, and clear performance standards to ensure programs are achieving their intended outcomes.

Government accountability means asking tough questions, demanding measurable results, and ensuring every dollar is properly managed. Washington residents deserve transparency, oversight, and leadership that prioritizes responsible stewardship of public funds.

Families in Federal Way deserve to feel safe walking our streets, visiting parks, and running local businesses. In recent years, the city has seen 534 violent crimes and 5,099 property crimes, which means roughly 1 in 200 residents could be affected each year. Crime isn’t just a threat to safety — it costs our community an estimated $84 million annually, or about $2,240 per household, through stolen property, damage, and the expenses of policing, courts, and jails.

​ Washington ranks 51st nationally in police officers per capita, with just 1.36 officers per 1,000 residents. That means fewer officers to respond quickly, patrol neighborhoods, and prevent crime proactively. I will support fully staffing our police, holding repeat offenders accountable, and ensuring behavioral health teams work alongside law enforcement to create safer streets.

​ Being a voice for public safety means advocating for resources, policies, and strategies that protect families, strengthen neighborhoods, and help local businesses thrive. Safer streets benefit everyone in our community.

pages.title: About | Mysite
paragraphs: I am a wife, a mom, and a small business owner. I am a homeschooling mom who is deeply involved in my daughter’s education and committed to making sure she has the best opportunities to learn and grow. Beyond my family, I am passionate about building community, supporting other small and local businesses, and helping families connect and thrive. Through volunteering, mentoring, and simply showing up for other parents and children, I see the challenges our community faces and the ways our voices are often not being heard. I want to bring attention to those issues and make sure families, children, and small businesses have a strong voice in local decision-making.

As a parent and small business owner in Federal Way, I live the realities many families are facing right now. The rising cost of living and growing financial strain are not minor issues. They impact our homes, our livelihoods, and the future we are working hard to build. I believe leadership should reflect the real experiences of the people it serves, and our community deserves representation that listens, asks tough questions, and stands up with clarity and accountability. That is why I am stepping forward to make sure families and local businesses have a strong voice at the table.

My mission is to represent our community and make sure our voices are heard in the decisions that shape our community. I am committed to showing up, listening, and ensuring those decisions reflect the people who live and work here. Together, we can build a community where every voice matters and every perspective is considered. I will work tirelessly to make sure our community’s needs and priorities are never overlooked.

pages.title: ISSUES | Kristine Reeves
paragraphs: As someone who was raised in poverty cycled in foster homes and was even homeless for a time, helping those in need is personal for me. I am not another lawyer or another multi-millionaire. Instead, I bring a unique perspective in that I understand what it means to struggle under tough circumstances, and that inspires my unwavering commitment to helping others struggling through tough times. I am committed to fighting every day to make sure that hard-working families never slip through the cracks.

As a working mother of two, I know firsthand the challenges of making our ends meet as gas and grocery prices skyrocket. I’m ready to take my work in economic development and my experience as a small business owner to work with business, state, and local governments and our residents to reduce the cost of household goods.

Progressive state policies I helped pass in the legislature, like the nation’s best Paid Family Medical Leave and a path towards more affordable child care, will help Washington families as we weather this crisis.

I also believe that expanding health care coverage and lowering medical and prescription drug costs will help promote income growth and stabilize our economy since it is often unforeseen health care events that can bankrupt struggling families. Making child care more accessible and affordable, ending the gender pay gap, raising the minimum wage and reinstating overtime rules, and enforcing and strengthening protections for organized labor that allow strong unions to flourish and effectively negotiate for workers – these are all important steps in chipping away at income inequality, ensuring the economic security of our families and promoting dignity and pride in the work we produce.

I’m very proud to have earned a 100% rating in the legislature from the Washington State Labor Council while helping guide the state to its ranking as one of the top economies in the country, proving that protecting and providing for our workforce goes hand in hand with a strong economy.

Every person in every neighborhood should feel safe in their homes and walking on the street. This means ensuring our first responders have the tools and resources to do their jobs. We need to expand community policing and community mental health officer programs so police have the assistance they need to respond the right way in the right situation to reduce crime and violence in our cities. We need to continue to build trust between our officers and the communities they serve.
As the mother of two children, I'm ready to work with the cities of Federal Way, Auburn, Algona, and Pacific to reduce crime in every neighborhood and on every street.

Childcare is essential. Now more than ever, families need safe, affordable, high-quality childcare to get our economy back on track. 63% of Washingtonians live in a childcare desert where there are either no childcare providers or 3 times as many children as licensed care spots. Working families will find a way for their kids to be cared for while they’re at work, but by not investing in licensed spots, they may be driven to find care on the unlicensed grey market with no safety standards. Now is the time to invest in facilities and workers that are supporting the reopening of our economy – by allowing the workforce to work. We must compensate childcare workers fairly, offer a stimulus and reopening grants for providers to offset new COVID-19 requirements, and create career pathways and financial aid for caregivers seeking early learning degrees. High-quality childcare builds America two generations at a time. This will require a unifying framework and national minimum standards for knowledge and competencies, educator qualifications, industry standards, and compensation that recognizes the professional nature and requirements of the industry. Health Care

I believe passionately that health care is a right for every person, not a privilege. I’ve spent much of my life with no health insurance coverage, and have a pre-existing health condition in diabetes that makes me acutely aware of, and like so many Americans, uniquely vulnerable to attacks that seek to deny health care coverage. I believe we need to do everything possible to make health care and prescription drugs more affordable. Our state is the first state in the country to plan for a public option for health care. I’m excited to make sure that plan reduces costs, increases transparency, and ensures accountability. Creating a public option will force insurance companies to compete, lowering health care costs for everyone.

I’m proud of our efforts in Washington state where we’ve established progressive models for the country in pursuit of these goals – we’ve cut the uninsured rate from 14% to nearly 5% thanks to an efficient and aggressive implementation of Obamacare, and we’ve established the country’s first long term care benefit that helps aging residents afford the care they need. These progressive policies that have improved the health and well-being of our citizens helped me earn a 100% rating from the Washington State Nurses Association while I served in the legislature.

Because of progressive public investments and caring mentors, I was able to escape the cycle of poverty. It was teachers who saved me, who guided me to overcome great childhood adversity and poverty, who cared enough to show me a path to success.

Every student deserves to have a quality public school in their community, and educators who can afford to live in the community they teach, so that we can prepare the next generation to succeed – no matter their ZIP code. I have fought for educators and for key investments that have strengthened the path to opportunity in our state – the biggest teacher salary increases in the nation, the largest-ever expansion of early childhood education, and linking tens of thousands of students with apprenticeships and on-the-job training.

Everyone should have access to an affordable college education if they choose, one that lets them pursue their dreams and a great career – without crushing debt from student loans. I speak from firsthand experience. With the help of a state need grant and scholarships, I was able to leave a childhood of poverty and tumult to become the first in my family to go to college and am today a proud Washington State graduate.

In my roles as Statewide Veterans Representative for U.S. Senator Patty Murray and Director of the Military Defense Sector in Governor Inslee’s Commerce Department, I have been connected to military families, employers and contractors in the South Sound on a daily basis.

My position as an advocate for military families and veterans is also shaped by my family. As the twin sister of a 17-year combat veteran in the United States Air Force, I can attest that the little brother that I sent off to war after 9/11 is not the man who came home. Our military service members put their lives on the line to defend our freedoms, and I am proud to be an outspoken advocate for service members and their families, making sure that they gain access to the opportunities and benefits that they’ve earned and deserve.

I have worked on veterans’ health care, improving military transition and workforce development, and have helped secure millions of dollars in federal grants to improve private-sector job growth, support military personnel transitioning to private-sector jobs, and support the 1900+ small businesses in the defense sector supply chain during Department of Defense downsizing.

I will continue to be a knowledgeable, compassionate and effective advocate for military families and veterans – from helping to reduce the suicide rate among veterans with better mental health treatment and services to better housing for military families to greater assistance in easing the transition between service and civilian careers. Climate Change
The changing climate is the defining challenge of my generation. It’s a threat to our economy, our way of life, and our entire existence.

As a working mom of two young kids, I think every day about the future our kids will have with our world literally on fire due to climate change. As someone who has worked on economic development, I understand the urgency and importance of comprehensive climate action and the repercussions of inaction. And as a woman of color, I know that too often front-line communities can be overlooked in the fight against climate change.

I’m proud to have been a part of Washington state’s bold leadership in combating the crisis. I was the primary sponsor of the Healthy Environments for All (HEAL) Act, which would require Washington state agencies to develop strategies to apply an environmental justice lens to their work and target investments in low income and communities of color – communities that are on the front-lines of pollution and health disparities.

I’m proud to have been a part of Washington state’s bold leadership in combating this crisis. We’ve established a Clean Energy Fund to grow well paid green jobs, we’ve built a $6 billion wind industry from scratch by incentivizing the private sector with renewable energy standards, and we passed a law to end Washington’s use of coal and shift our state to use 100% clean energy to generate electricity.

I believe Washington State must take a leadership role in addressing climate change, not only to protect ourselves from threats like hurricanes and wildfires that increasingly threaten our daily lives and resources but because we must take advantage of the economic opportunity that exists to be a leader in the creation of clean energy jobs and the next generation of economic innovation.

pages.title: ABOUT KRISTINE | Kristine Reeves
paragraphs: Kristine grew up the daughter of a single mother who struggled with substance abuse and relied heavily on social services including Head Start and food stamps. In and out of foster care and even homeless at points in her childhood, Kristine’s journey to elected state representative, a Director of Economic Development in the Commerce Department, and happily married mother of two children is a testimony to the value of public education and the critical investment of public-school educators in transforming her life and helping her break the cycle of poverty. The first in her family to graduate from college, Kristine received her bachelor’s degree in Political Science from Washington State University (Go Cougs!) and a master’s degree in Organizational Leadership from Gonzaga University in Spokane.

Kristine is the daughter, granddaughter and twin sister of veterans, which fuels her passion for military families. She has served the state as an immigration advisor to several higher education institutions helping hundreds of international students pursue education opportunities in the United States. Then as the South Sound Regional Director and Statewide Veterans Representative for US Senator Patty Murray, she worked on veterans’ health care, improving military transition and workforce development. She worked for 6.5 years in the Washington Commerce Department as the Director of the Military and Defense Sector, where she helped foster economic opportunities for military families, veterans, and the community. In this role, Kristine helped secure millions of dollars in federal grants to improve private sector job growth, supported military personnel transitioning to private sector jobs, and supported the 1900+ small businesses in the defense sector supply chain during the Department of Defense downsizing.
Kristine’s hard work combined with a unique background and professional perspective played an important role in multiple achievements that have provided a national model for progressive action:
ensuring educators can afford to live and work in the communities in which they teach our kids
launching a Career Connect program that’s linking tens of thousands of students with apprenticeships and on-the-job training
passing the country’s most progressive paid family leave policy to care for loved ones or newborns
creating the country’s first long term health care benefit to help seniors stay in their homes
pushing for the state’s first environmental justice directive to combat climate change and protect communities of color
leading the effort to make childcare more accessible and affordable for ALL working families

Kristine is the mom to two amazing kiddos and is married to her longtime sweetheart Camron. In 2016 Kristine was the first African American woman elected to the Washington House in 18 years, and the only woman in the legislature with children under the age of 5.

pages.title: Paul 4 Washington - Virtue, Faith, & Freedom
paragraphs: Families are working harder than ever, yet too many are struggling to keep up with rising taxes, higher housing costs, public safety concerns, and an education system that is falling short of preparing our children for the future.
I believe government should work for the people—not the other way around.

As a Marine Corps veteran, small business owner, community volunteer, and former Federal Way City Councilmember, I have spent my life solving problems, serving others, and bringing people together. I'm running for the Washington State House because I believe we can build a safer, more affordable, and more prosperous future for every family in the 30th Legislative District.
Together, we can build a stronger Washington.
Everywhere I go, I hear the same concerns.
These challenges aren't unique to one city or one political party. They affect all of us.
I'm running because I believe government should focus on practical solutions, responsible leadership, and creating opportunities for every Washington family to succeed.
It needs leaders willing to listen, learn, and make thoughtful decisions based on facts, accountability, and common sense.
Families are worried about the rising cost of living.
Neighborhoods want safer bus stops and streets.
Young adults & families wonder if they'll ever be able to afford a home.
Parents are concerned about their children's future.
Business owners are struggling with ever-increasing taxes and regulations.
Before entering public office, I spent decades serving my community in other ways.
As a young entrepreneur, I built a technology consulting business from the ground up and learned firsthand what it takes to meet payroll, balance budgets, and adapt through economic uncertainty.
As a United States Marine Corps veteran, I learned that leadership begins with service, discipline, and responsibility.
As a community volunteer, youth mentor, and martial arts instructor, I've worked alongside families, students, and local organizations to help build stronger communities.

My appointment to the Federal Way City Council deepened my understanding of how government works—and where it can work better. It reinforced my belief that good policy starts with listening to the people we serve.
Public office isn't a career goal for me. It's another opportunity to serve.
Washington families deserve a government that lives within its means.
I support reducing unnecessary tax burdens, increasing transparency, and making government more accountable to taxpayers.
Every family deserves to feel safe at home, at work, and in their neighborhood.
I'll support law enforcement, improve public safety, and expand effective treatment options that address addiction and mental health while holding criminals accountable.
Healthy communities begin with strong families.
I believe government should strengthen—not replace—the family by supporting policies that promote stability, opportunity, and personal responsibility.
Owning a home and earning a family-wage income should once again be realistic goals for hardworking residents.
I'll work to remove unnecessary barriers to housing and encourage economic growth through business-friendly policies.
Parents are their children's first teachers and strongest advocates.
Every student deserves access to a quality education that prepares them for the workforce, skilled trades, military service, or college.
I believe Washington's best days are still ahead.

With responsible leadership, fiscal accountability, safer communities, strong families, quality education, and expanded economic opportunity, we can build a future where every person willing to work has the opportunity to succeed.
I'd be honored to earn your trust, your support, and your vote for State Representative. T ogether, let's build a stronger Washington!

pages.title: Issues - Paul 4 Washington
paragraphs: Every challenge facing Washington is connected. Our solutions should be, too.
Washington is a remarkable place to live, work, raise a family, and build a business. Yet many Washington families are asking difficult questions.
Will our children have greater opportunities than we did?
Can we trust government to spend our tax dollars wisely?

These are not isolated issues. They are connected. The decisions we make about taxes influence housing. Education affects workforce development. Public safety impacts economic growth. Government accountability builds public trust. Strong families strengthen every community.
Real leadership recognizes these connections and develops solutions that address both today's challenges and tomorrow's opportunities.
That is the approach I will bring to Olympia.
Listen First. Lead with Facts. Focus on Results.
Good public policy begins with listening.
Before proposing solutions, leaders must understand the challenges facing the people they represent.

Throughout this campaign, I have met with residents, business owners, educators, first responders, nonprofit organizations, labor representatives, veterans, community leaders, and local officials across our district.
These priorities should guide every decision made in Olympia. Good government is not measured by how many bills it passed or how much it spends. It is measured by the results it delivers.
Although each conversation is unique, several themes consistently emerge .
Families want to keep more of what they earn.
Communities want safer neighborhoods, streets, and bus stops.
Young adults want the chance to buy their first home.
Businesses want the opportunity to grow.
Seniors want to remain in the communities they helped build.

pages.title: Fiscal Responsibility - Paul 4 Washington
paragraphs: Hardworking families across Washington are making difficult financial decisions every day.
They're adjusting household budgets, delaying major purchases, working extra hours, and finding ways to stretch every dollar. Government should be held to that same standard.

As your State Representative, I will work to reduce unnecessary taxes, improve government accountability, eliminate wasteful spending, and ensure taxpayer dollars are focused on the core responsibilities of state government.
Responsible government isn't about spending less simply for the sake of spending less. It's about spending smarter.

Families throughout the 30th Legislative District are feeling the pressure. The cost of housing continues to climb. Groceries cost more. Gas prices remain volatile. Insurance premiums continue to rise. Utility bills continue to increase. Small businesses face growing regulatory costs.
At the same time, state government continues to expand its spending while asking taxpayers to shoulder an ever-growing financial burden.
Government should never forget whose money it is spending. Every dollar collected in taxes belongs first to the people who earned it.
Government has an important role. It should provide essential services.
But government also has an obligation to respect taxpayers. That means asking difficult questions before creating new taxes.
Can we spend existing dollars more effectively?
Are programs producing measurable results?
These are the questions government should ask before asking taxpayers for more money.
Washington families already face one of the highest overall tax burdens in the nation when state and local taxes, fees, and assessments are combined.
I will oppose efforts to create a state personal income tax for anyone and work to protect Washington's long-standing approach to taxation.
Many professional services have become increasingly expensive for families and small businesses.
Expanding sales taxes into additional services makes it harder to start businesses, hire professionals, and grow our economy.
I support eliminating the sales tax on services to reduce costs and encourage economic growth.
Taxes on products such as tobacco, vapor products, and alcohol often fall disproportionately on lower-income residents while generating increasingly unstable revenue.
I support reviewing these taxes and reducing excessive rates where appropriate, while ensuring that public health objectives remain part of the conversation.
Washington's Business & Occupation (B&O) Tax often requires businesses to pay taxes on gross revenue—even when they have little or no profit.
That structure can make it harder for entrepreneurs and small businesses to survive.
I support a comprehensive review of the B&O tax to identify reforms that encourage investment, job creation, and long-term economic growth.
For many homeowners, property taxes continue to rise faster than household incomes.
For renters, increasing property taxes often contribute to higher housing costs.
I support reviewing state property tax policies to identify opportunities to provide meaningful relief while protecting essential local services.
Before asking taxpayers for additional revenue, state government should first examine whether existing resources are being used effectively.
My approach to budgeting follows the same principles successful families and businesses use every day.
Second, identify essential responsibilities.
Finally, evaluate programs based on measurable outcomes—not political popularity.
Government should regularly review existing programs to determine whether they continue delivering value to taxpayers.
Good government depends on public trust. That trust requires transparency.
I support making government easier to understand by expanding public access to:
Taxpayers shouldn't need to file public records requests simply to understand how their money is being spent.
Washington must also become one of the best places in America to start and grow a business.
Investing in infrastructure that supports commerce
More businesses create more jobs. More jobs create more opportunities. More opportunities strengthen families.
Because affordability affects nearly every issue facing Washington families.
Lowering unnecessary tax burdens allows families to keep more of what they earn while encouraging economic growth.
Yes—but it requires setting clear priorities, eliminating waste, improving efficiency, and evaluating whether programs are achieving measurable results before expanding government spending.
It means government that is effective, accountable, transparent, and focused on its core responsibilities.
Small businesses create jobs, invest in local communities, support nonprofit organizations, and drive economic growth throughout Washington.
When small businesses succeed, communities succeed.

pages.title: Public Safety - Paul 4 Washington
paragraphs: Every Washington family deserves to feel safe at home, at work, at school, and in their community.
Public safety is one of government's most fundamental responsibilities.

Families should feel comfortable walking through their neighborhoods and at bus stops. Children should be able to learn in safe schools. Businesses should not have to accept theft and vandalism as simply "the cost of doing business." Police officers should have the tools they need to protect our communities. And individuals struggling with addiction or mental illness should have access to treatment that helps them rebuild their lives.
A safer Washington requires accountability, compassion, and common sense working together.

As your State Representative, I will support policies that restore public confidence, strengthen our justice system, support law enforcement, and expand effective solutions that reduce crime over the long term.
Across Washington, residents continue to express concerns about public safety.

Parents worry about violence in and around schools. Business owners invest thousands of dollars replacing broken windows, repairing vandalism, and preventing theft. Neighborhoods are experiencing increased concerns about drug activity, property crime, and repeat offenders. Law enforcement agencies face staffing shortages while responding to increasingly complex situations involving mental illness, addiction, and homelessness.

At the same time, many people struggling with addiction or behavioral health challenges are caught in a cycle of crisis that neither the criminal justice system nor existing treatment programs have fully addressed.
We must build a system that protects victims, holds offenders accountable, and provides meaningful opportunities for rehabilitation when appropriate.
Public safety is not about choosing between enforcement and treatment. It requires both.

Some individuals repeatedly choose to victimize others. Others struggle because of addiction, untreated mental illness, trauma, or circumstances that require a different response. Government should recognize the difference. A one-size-fits-all approach serves no one well.
Our goal should be to reduce crime, improve public safety, and help as many people as possible become productive members of society.
It's not about being tougher. It's not about being softer. It's about being smarter.
Our police officers perform one of the most difficult jobs in public service.
They deserve the training, staffing, equipment, legal clarity, and community support necessary to protect our neighborhoods.
Recruiting and retaining qualified law enforcement officers.
Providing modern training and equipment.
Strengthening cooperation between local, county, tribal, and state agencies.
Giving officers clear laws and policies they can confidently enforce.
Supporting community policing efforts that build trust between officers and residents.
Public safety begins with ensuring those responsible for protecting our communities have the tools they need to succeed.
Not every public safety challenge begins with criminal intent.
Many involve untreated addiction, mental illness, or unresolved trauma. For these individuals, treatment is often the most effective long-term public safety strategy.
Treatment is not an alternative to accountability. It is often the path toward restoring personal responsibility .
One of the most effective ways to reduce crime is to prevent it.
