Young people who have positive mentors, safe activities, and meaningful opportunities are far less likely to enter the criminal justice system.
Young people need hope, purpose, and opportunity. Communities benefit when we invest in all three.
Too often, discussions about public safety focus only on offenders. Victims deserve equal attention.
Protecting victims is one of government's highest responsibilities.
Most people deserve the opportunity to learn from mistakes.
However, individuals who repeatedly commit violent crimes or continually victimize others must face meaningful consequences.
Victims deserve justice. Communities deserve protection.
I support policies that improve communication between law enforcement, prosecutors, courts, and correctional agencies so that repeat offenders are identified early and handled appropriately.
Accountability protects both current and future victims.
One lesson from both business and local government is that better information leads to better decisions.
Our justice system works best when decision-makers have accurate, timely information.

Within appropriate legal and privacy protections, I support improving coordination between agencies so judges, prosecutors, law enforcement, and treatment providers have the information necessary to make informed decisions about supervision, sentencing, treatment, and public safety.
Better data can help distinguish between those who pose an ongoing threat to the community and those who are most likely to succeed through treatment and structured support.
Smarter decisions create safer communities.

I believe law enforcement officers deserve the staffing, training, legal clarity, and community support necessary to perform their duties effectively while remaining accountable to the communities they serve.
Some individuals require incarceration to protect the public.
Others are more likely to reduce future criminal behavior through treatment, supervision, and support.
The goal should always be the approach most likely to improve public safety.
Homelessness is a complex issue involving housing, behavioral health, addiction, employment, and personal circumstances.
Solutions should address the underlying causes while maintaining safe and welcoming public spaces for everyone.
Government cannot create safe neighborhoods by itself.
Families, schools, nonprofits, businesses, faith organizations, and engaged citizens all play essential roles in preventing crime and supporting recovery.
Safer communities begin with engaged citizens.
Attend neighborhood meetings. Support youth mentoring. Volunteer with community organizations. Report criminal activity. Support first responders. Look out for your neighbors.
Together, we can create communities where every family feels safe.

pages.title: Housing & Jobs - Paul 4 Washington
paragraphs: Building a Washington where hard work makes homeownership and financial security possible again.
For generations, Washington was a place where families could build a career, buy a home, raise children, and retire with confidence.

Today, that dream feels increasingly out of reach for many people. Young adults question whether they'll ever own a home. Working families spend a growing share of their income on housing. Employers struggle to fill positions because workers can't afford to live nearby. Small businesses face rising costs while competing for employees in an increasingly expensive market.

As your State Representative, I will support policies that expand housing opportunities, encourage job creation, strengthen small businesses, and help restore the promise that hard work leads to a better future.
Housing affordability and economic opportunity are among the greatest challenges facing Washington today.

Families are working harder but often falling behind. The cost of purchasing a home has increased dramatically. Rental prices continue to rise. Construction costs remain high. Permitting processes are often lengthy and unpredictable. At the same time, many employers struggle to recruit workers because housing near available jobs has become increasingly unaffordable.
These challenges affect every generation.

Young adults delay starting families. Working parents spend less time together because of longer commutes or second jobs. Seniors worry about remaining in the communities they helped build. Employers lose opportunities to grow. Communities lose the people who make them strong.
Housing and jobs are not separate issues. They rise—or fall—together.
The American dream has never been guaranteed. But it has always been built on opportunity.
People who work hard, save, invest, and contribute to their communities should have a realistic chance to achieve financial security and homeownership.
Government cannot create prosperity. But it can create an environment where prosperity becomes more attainable.
That means encouraging private investment, removing unnecessary barriers, supporting entrepreneurship, and ensuring government policies help—not hinder—economic growth.
Strong communities are built when people have the opportunity to work, build businesses, purchase homes, and invest in their neighborhoods.
Washington needs more housing. Not just one type of housing.
We need a diverse mix of housing options that meet the needs of young adults, growing families, seniors, veterans, and individuals with disabilities.
Accessory dwelling units where appropriate
Redevelopment of underutilized properties
Public-private partnerships that increase housing availability
More housing options create healthier, more affordable communities.
Small businesses are the backbone of Washington's economy.

As a small business owner, I understand the challenges entrepreneurs face because I've lived them. I've balanced budgets. Made payroll. Navigated economic downturns. Adapted to changing technology. Managed rising operating costs.
Government should make it easier—not harder—for people to start, grow, and sustain successful businesses.
When small businesses succeed, communities prosper.
Washington has become a global leader in technology, aerospace, agriculture, manufacturing, healthcare, and research.
We should continue creating an environment that encourages innovation while ensuring opportunities exist throughout every region of the state.
Innovation creates jobs. Jobs create opportunity. Opportunity strengthens families.
Unnecessary delays increase construction costs, discourage investment, and ultimately raise housing prices for everyone.
I support modernizing permitting processes by:
Increasing transparency throughout the review process
Holding government accountable for predictable timelines
Protecting public safety and environmental standards should remain essential, but efficiency and accountability should be equally important.
Washington's economy is changing rapidly.
We must prepare students and workers for careers that will exist not only today, but decades into the future.
Every student should graduate with a pathway to success.
Whether that path leads to the workforce, skilled trades, military service, entrepreneurship, or college, every option deserves equal respect.
A home represents far more than four walls and a roof.
It is where children grow. Families gather. Neighbors become friends. Communities take root.
Stable housing contributes to stronger educational outcomes, improved health, reduced crime, and greater civic engagement.
Expanding housing opportunities isn't simply an economic issue. It's a community issue.
When businesses succeed, communities benefit.

New jobs create new opportunities. Higher incomes strengthen families. Increased investment revitalizes neighborhoods. Local businesses support schools, nonprofits, youth sports, and community organizations.
Economic growth should never be measured only in dollars. It should also be measured by the opportunities it creates for the people who call Washington home.
People need stable employment to afford housing, and employers need affordable housing nearby to recruit and retain workers.
Government has an important role in planning, infrastructure, and establishing fair regulations, but lasting housing solutions require collaboration between the public and private sectors.
My focus is on creating an environment that encourages responsible development while protecting the quality of our communities.
Small businesses employ thousands of Washington residents, invest locally, support community organizations, and create opportunities for future entrepreneurs.
They deserve policies that encourage success rather than unnecessary barriers.
The skilled trades are essential to Washington's future.
Electricians, plumbers, carpenters, mechanics, healthcare workers, manufacturers, and countless other professionals build and maintain the communities we depend on every day.
Career education should receive the same respect as traditional college pathways.
Creating opportunity requires all of us.

Support local businesses. Mentor young entrepreneurs. Hire apprentices. Volunteer with workforce development programs. Attend community planning meetings. Invest in your neighborhood. Encourage innovation.
Together, we can create communities where families have the opportunity to work, succeed, and build a future.

pages.title: Education - Paul 4 Washington
paragraphs: Every child deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, and graduate prepared for the future they choose.
Education is one of the most important investments we make—not only in our children, but in the future of Washington.
Students deserve safe schools, excellent teachers, and learning environments that challenge them to reach their full potential.
Parents deserve meaningful involvement in their children's education.
Teachers deserve respect, support, and the resources necessary to help students succeed.
Communities deserve schools that prepare young people for college, the skilled trades, military service, entrepreneurship, and meaningful careers.
As your State Representative, I will support policies that strengthen educational opportunity, improve academic achievement, and prepare every student for success in an ever-changing world.
Education is changing. Technology is changing. The workforce is changing.

The skills students will need twenty years from now may be very different from those required today. At the same time, many parents continue to express concerns about academic performance, school safety, transparency, classroom resources, and student well-being.
Teachers face increasing responsibilities while balancing limited time and resources.
Employers often report difficulty finding workers with the technical, communication, and problem-solving skills needed for today's economy.
These challenges require thoughtful leadership focused on student success rather than political division.
Education should prepare young people for life.

Every child learns differently and each student follows a different path. Some will attend college. Others will enter the skilled trades. Some will join the military. Others will become entrepreneurs.
Each path deserves equal respect. The purpose of education is not to prepare every student for the same future. It is to prepare every student for their future.
Government should establish high expectations while allowing schools, educators, parents, and local communities the flexibility to help students achieve them.

Parents are a child's first teachers. Their involvement does not end when their child enters the classroom. Strong schools are built through partnerships between parents, teachers, administrators, and students.
Open communication between schools and families
Transparency regarding academic progress
When schools and families work together, students benefit.
Every student deserves an education that builds a strong foundation in:
These core skills prepare students to succeed regardless of the career path they ultimately choose.
Academic excellence should remain the foundation of public education.
Not every successful career begins with a four-year college degree.
Career and Technical Education (CTE), apprenticeships, internships, and industry partnerships provide valuable pathways toward successful careers.
Students should graduate with opportunities—not unnecessary debt.
Public education remains one of the most important responsibilities of state government.
Our goal should always be helping every student succeed while supporting teachers, parents, and local communities.
Career education should receive the same respect as traditional college preparation.
Students should have multiple pathways toward successful and rewarding careers.
Parents are essential partners in education.
Schools are strongest when educators and families communicate openly and work together in support of student success.
Education and economic opportunity are closely connected.
Preparing students for meaningful careers strengthens families, businesses, and communities throughout Washington.
Great schools are built through community involvement.
Volunteer at a school. Mentor a student. Support teachers. Attend school board meetings. Encourage reading. Partner with local businesses. Invest in youth programs. Celebrate student success.
Every community has a role in preparing the next generation.
Together, we can build a stronger Washington

pages.title: Home - Phil Fortunato for Senate
paragraphs: Thank you for visiting and for believing in the power of common-sense leadership. Washington needs strong, principled voices who will stand up for hardworking families, protect your freedoms, and fight for safe communities.

Throughout my time in the State Senate, I’ve never backed down from a challenge, and I’ve never forgotten who I work for: you . Whether it’s pushing back against government overreach, defending parental rights, or advocating for real solutions to crime and homelessness, I’ve remained focused on what matters most: results.

My campaign is about restoring accountability, empowering citizens, and putting people first. Together, we can keep fighting for a future where families thrive, small businesses grow, and the government respects your values.
I invite you to join our team, share your ideas, and help us move Washington in the right direction. Let’s keep up the fight, together.

pages.title: About Me - Phil Fortunato for Senate
paragraphs: I have been married to my wife, Suzanne for over 45 years. We have five children and 4 grandchildren. Three of our sons joined U.S. Marines and our oldest retired after 20 years. My wife and I live in Auburn, Washington. I’m active in my local church and work in support of charity efforts in the community.

I started my first business at the age of 18, and what started as a side-job cutting grass for friends and neighbors evolved into a commercial landscaping company. Since then, I started my own hydroseeding and landscaping company which I ran for a number of years before founding my current venture: Eco-3, an erosion and stormwater management company. With over 30 years of experience in erosion control and stormwater management, I provide environmental training and help builders navigate environmental regulation. I was president and founding director of the Pacific Northwest chapter of the International Erosion Control Association.

I currently serve as the 31st District State Senator. I was elected to the House of Representatives in 2016 and appointed to the Senate before being sworn into the House. I won re-election in 2022 to a 4-year term that expires in 2026. I previously served as the 47th District State Representative from 1998 to 2000. I’m focused on a number of policy issues, serving on the State Government and Elections Committee, Transportation Committee, Housing Committee, and Environmental Committee in the state Senate.

pages.title: Together with Tamara
paragraphs: From Canvassing to sign waving, hosting a house party and more! Sign-up to get involved and join our campaign
It’s time we have leadership that cares deeply about middle-class families, invests in education, and takes rural infrastructure seriously.
I’m ready to represent the full 31st District with honesty, compassion, and determination.
Kristin Reeves , WA State Representative
Kate Baldwin , City of Auburn Councilmember
Stephanie Vignal , City of Mill Creek Mayor
Griselda Arias , City of Yelm Councilmember
Cheryl Rakes , City of Auburn Councilmember
Make sure you’re getting the latest campaign updates and developments by following the official Together with Tamara pages on Instagram and Facebook.
Tamara Stramel (@ together_with_tamara ) • Instagram photos and videos

pages.title: Meet Tamara our next State Senator in the 31st
paragraphs: I. Rising Costs: Gas, Groceries & Utilities II. Infrastructure Investments III. Education
Utilities have jumped by 30%. Our children can’t afford to live where they grew up. The cost to drive is outrageous. You deserve someone who takes these issues seriously.
I will work to stop price gouging by supporting laws to prohibit surveillance and surge pricing that take advantage of customers.
I will explore public transportation and private solutions to reduce costs and shorten commute times.
I will focus on the shortage of available, affordable homes for smaller households – from young families to empty nesters.
I will ensure the funding for the Fairfax Bridge is secured and bring good union wages to the local workers who build the replacement.
I will work with regional cities to inventory critical routes and make sure we prevent bridge failures and road closures that hurt families and businesses.
I will bring home funding for flood mitigation solutions to protect our communities.
Our infrastructure must match our growth. We need to be able to commute safely and easily across the region and ensure we preserve the beauty and convenience that drew us to these communities.
As a local Mom and champion for public education, I will work tirelessly to improve every aspect of our schools when im elected.
Will work to change our broken funding model when elected. Unfunded regulations are hurting our local schools, we need to have a realistic funding model to get our kids the best education.
I know how important good meals and nutrition are for our kids. I will fight to expand the free school meals program to all schools.

pages.title: Meet Tamara our next State Senator in the 31st
paragraphs: Ready to represent the 31st District with honesty, compassion, and determination.

After being born and raised in Nevada and traveling the country throughout my twenties, my family and I chose Pierce County, Washington, as the place to plant roots. Since 2018, we’ve called the Lake Tapps area home and are deeply grateful to live in such a beautiful, community-focused place.
I earned a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from California State University, Bakersfield, and spent my early career working with at-risk and incarcerated youth in residential programs.

I served both in direct care and leadership roles, including in outdoor experiential education programs in North Carolina, Florida, and New Hampshire — work that shaped my lifelong commitment to equity, accountability, and service.

During my husband’s military service, I helped reestablish the Family Readiness Group (FRG) for the USS Shoup (DDG 86), creating a vital network of support for military families during deployments and transitions.

After his military service, we settled in Lake Tapps with our two children. As a parent and active volunteer, I’ve served on our local PTA board, chaired school events like the book fair, and supported school and community initiatives aimed at building strong, transparent systems. I was proud to help organize the successful campaign for the Sumner-Bonney Lake School Bond — the largest school bond in Washington State history to pass. I now volunteer on the Oversight Committee for that bond, working to ensure public transparency and fiscal accountability.
When I’m not involved in local efforts, I enjoy reading, hiking, camping, and distance swimming — and reminding everyone I meet how important it is to participate in local government and vote!

pages.title: Issues - Re-Elect Drew Stokesbary
paragraphs: I have served on the House Finance Committee for all three of my terms in the State House. There I have helped defeat tens of billions of dollars worth of new taxes proposed by the Governor and majority-party Democrats, including new or additional taxes on income you earn, energy you consume, bottled water you drink, services you hire professionals to perform, the house you sell, the car you trade in, and the things you buy on the internet.

Since I was first elected in 2014, biennial state general fund spending was $33 billion. Now the budget has ballooned to well over $50 billion, an increase of nearly 70 percent increase in just six years. (Has your own household income risen by 70 percent since 2014?) With our economy struggling from coronavirus and the risk of a recession, or even a full-fledged depression, higher than ever, now is not the time to continue raising taxes.

Instead of more taxes, the Legislature needs to better prioritize state spending. As the chief budget writer for the House Republicans, I’ve worked hard to identify and eliminate waste, fraud and abuse, but far more remains to be done. We must also reform our state budget process to avoid committing to such large and rapid spending increases. I’ll continue pushing for these reforms if I’m re-elected.

As Washington recovers from this unprecedented public health crisis, I want to ensure the economy is opened quickly but safely and there is an opportunity for all Washingtonians to be successful. That’s why the latest idea out of Seattle, to levy a tax on businesses for employees they hire, is so misguided. In Olympia, I’ll continue to advocate for policies that grow the economy and create jobs, not ones that disincentive hiring.

In the Legislature, I have fought to increase funding for law enforcement and firefighting activities. I’ve also advocated for reforms that will allow local jurisdictions to deliver services more efficiently, which helps deliver more services while saving taxpayers money. For my work, I was named an Honorary Fire Chief and “legislator of the year” by the Washington Fire Chiefs Association .

My mom was a teacher in Washington State for 25 years, and her father was a teacher before that. My dad’s parents both taught at the Washington State School for the Deaf. Coming from a family of teachers, I’ve always understood the importance of quality education. I’m proud to have been endorsed by Public School Employees of Washington, the union representing 30,000+ educators and other K-12 school support professionals.

As a father of two young boys, I want good schools more than ever. Schools should have the resources they need to succeed, and we must ensure those resources are used wisely. That’s why I’ve been endorsed once again by Stand for Children , an organization that, like me, “strives to ensure that all children, regardless of their background, graduate high school prepared for, and with access to, college or career training.”

When I was first elected to the Legislature in 2014, the state had already been held in “contempt of court” for failing to constitutionally fund K-12 public schools. A few months later, the Supreme Court ordered a $100,000 per day fine until education was fully funded. Through my work on the House Appropriations and Education Committees and other bipartisan negotiations, I’m proud to have helped create and pass landmark education funding reform legislation in 2017. The new system dramatically increased funding for Auburn, Enumclaw, Sumner, White River, Carbonado and Dieringer School Districts (while still reducing total property taxes for those districts starting next year), increases the accountability and transparency of your tax dollars, and ensures K-12 funds are spent on things that matter like textbooks and smaller class sizes.
Kids deserve our first dollar, not our last dime. I will continue be your advocate for better schools and better outcomes.

In addition to the countless individuals and organizations who have endorsed his reelection campaign , Rep. Stokesbary’s hard work in the Legislature on behalf of the residents of the 31st District has earned special recognition by several groups:
Recipient of the June Robinson Public Health Funding Award by the Washington State Public Health Association, for his work securing public health funding before and during COVID-19
Winner of the City Champion Award from the Association of Washington Cities for helping to develop solutions to solve the budgetary challenges of cities
Named Honorary Fire Chief by the Washington Fire Chiefs for his for his work in Olympia to preserve and improve fire services
Winner of City Champion Award from Association of Washington Cities for his work on comprehensive police “body cam” legislation
Recipient of “In The Bag” Award from Washington Food Industry Association for his work on behalf of local, independent grocery stores
Rep. Stokesbary has already been the prime sponsor of five bills signed into law by the Governor:
HB 1467 improves fire service efficiencies so departments can reduce overhead costs and deliver more services instead
HB 1940 protects funding for the King and Pierce County flood control districts so they have the resources to continue combatting floods along the Green, White, Puyallup, and Carbon Rivers
HB 1637 helps combat the rising opioid epidemic by allowing tribal law enforcement agencies access to the state’s prescription drug monitoring database
HB 2320 saves Emerald Downs from potential temporary shutdowns, which helps boost the Auburn economy
HB 1253 streamlines regulations for many small businesses who had been regulated by two separate state agencies

Rep. Stokesbary also introduced HB 1427, which would have expanded the property tax exemption available to fixed-income retirees and veterans . The Legislature ultimately passed a similar Senate bill , which the Governor signed in 2015.
Rep. Stokesbary has worked with senior legislators on both sides of the aisle to fund capital projects that make our neighborhoods a great place to live, work and raise a family:
New and modernized schools in Auburn , Carbonado , Sumner , and White River School Districts
More homeless shelter beds for Nexus Youth and Families in Auburn (formerly (Auburn Youth Resources)
A new drug rehabilitation facility in Auburn , operated by Valley Cities Counseling
Upgraded facilities at Rainier State School in Buckley
Completion of the brand-new Gordon Family YMCA in Sumner
Improvements, repairs, and maintenance at the Enumclaw Expo Center
Flood control projects along the Green River (north of Enumclaw ), White River (in Sumner ), Puyallup River (between Sumner and Orting ), and Carbon River (from Carbonado to Orting )
Phase 1 of a brand-new Edgewood Community Park
Additional extensions of the Foothills Trail in South Prairie , Sumner , and Buckley , connecting the trail to Enumclaw
Improvements to Roosevelt Park in Wilkeson
New storage facilities for the Daffodil Heritage Parade in Sumner
In addition, Rep. Stokesbary has sponsored or co-sponsored several other important bills to keep our communities safe:
HB 1761 to prevent King County or other municipalities from opening “heroin injection sites”
HB 2545 bans the use of several known toxic chemicals in children’s toys and clothing
HB 1281 expands a successful tri-county child pornography task force to cover the entire state

Rep. Stokesbary has worked diligently to successfully obtain funding for several badly-needed transportation projects in our communities. These projects will decrease travel times, increase safety, and give families more time to spend together:
Final completion of a freeway (Highway 167) between Puyallup and Tacoma , which had been promised to residents by WSDOT and the Legislature for over 30 years

Construction of a new eastbound Highway 18 off-ramp and a bypass around Auburn Way South , which will reduce congestion on Highway 18 and decrease travel times to South Auburn and the Enumclaw Plateau
Design and engineering of a new, wider Traffic Avenue bridge over Highway 410 in Sumner , which will greatly reduce the long rush hour backups going in and out of Sumner
Construction of a seismic wall along Jovita Boulevard in Edgewood , which will protect the integrity of this important thoroughfare even in a significant earthquake

pages.title: Meet Drew - Re-Elect Drew Stokesbary
paragraphs: Rep. Drew Stokesbary was born and raised here in the Puget Sound area, growing up in the shadow of Mt. Rainier and graduating from a local public high school.

He earned a Bachelor of Science in Economics from Duke University, where he also studied Mathematics and History, before returning home to Washington. Inspired by leaders like Rob McKenna and Slade Gorton, Drew enrolled in law school at the University of Notre Dame, eventually graduating cum laude . After law school, Drew moved back home to Auburn, passed the bar exam and spent several years serving as policy aide for a King County Councilmember.

When a seat in the State Legislature opened up, Drew was encouraged to run by local leaders, eventually winning with over 60 percent of the vote as first-time candidate. He was elected to caucus leadership by his colleagues at the beginning of his second term and later served as Minority Floor Leader, Ranking Member on the House Appropriations Committee and Chair of the Select Committee on Pension Policy. Since 2023, he has served as House Minority Leader.

Outside of the Legislature, Drew is an attorney. He is currently a partner at the boutique law firm Chalmers, Adams, Backer & Kaufman, where he provides corporate and securities law counsel to startups and emerging companies in the Puget Sound region and around the world. He has also represented clients on constitutional matters, including cases throughout the country involving redistricting, ballot access and election canvassing, has authored numerous Supreme Court briefs, and served as outside counsel to leading candidates for President, U.S. Senate, Congress and Governor. During the pandemic, Drew co-founded Citizen Action Defense Fund, a nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting the constitutional rights of all Washingtonians. He is also a volunteer member of the Board of Directors of the Auburn Valley YMCA.

Drew has been married to his wife Ashley for over 15 years. Together they have four sons between the ages of 10 and 1, and a fetch-obsessed border collie. When Drew isn’t working, he enjoys cooking, watching his sons play soccer, and hiking and camping throughout Washington with his family.

pages.title: Stephen Szczurko-Walton — Running for WA State House (LD-31)
paragraphs: Running for State Representative (D) — Legislative District 31
Universal healthcare, a progressive tax structure, and state preemption — to bring down the costs putting life out of reach.
Eliminate corporate money from our elections — starting with SB 6358 to bypass Citizens United.
A stronger Utilities and Transportation Commission, a modernized grid, and every safe, clean power source on the table.
No noise. Just where we’ll be and what’s at stake.
This seat is winnable. It comes down to who shows up.

pages.title: Issues – Stephen for District 31
paragraphs: Three pillars. Plain statements, not policy walls.
Universal healthcare, a state income tax, and state preemption — to bring down the costs putting life out of reach.

We are living through an affordability crisis we haven’t seen in decades. Groceries, rent, and property taxes are climbing faster than paychecks across the 31st. Raw materials for housing are up, putting homes more out of reach. And the gutting of Medicaid and the ACA is sending healthcare premiums higher — people are falling through the cracks.
Universal healthcare — more effective than the private insurance market, and the only path that lifts the employer-tied premium drag off working families.

A progressive tax structure that ends Washington’s status as the second-most-regressive tax state in the country, where the lowest-income households currently pay five times the share of income that the wealthiest do.
State preemption to cut red tape on housing construction, so working families have a real path to ownership.

Trust is earned in public. That means plain rules, open books, and a representative who explains the vote before it happens — not after. Citizens United may be the law of the land — for now — but Washington can do something about it.
Work to get corporate money out of Washington elections, starting with SB 6358.

SB 6358 would bypass Citizens United and remove status for any non-human entity — corporation, union, non-profit — that spends money to sway an election in Washington State. From day one, I would work ceaselessly to get SB 6358 passed, even if it means going to other senators’ districts to talk to their constituents all around the state.

Energy is foundational to modern life — people in hospitals on life support, homes and schools that need heat in the winter. But the demands on our grid are changing fast, from new data centers to growing communities, and working families are the ones who pay when the system doesn’t keep up.

Give the Utilities and Transportation Commission real authority to keep pace with how fast our energy needs are changing — and the staffing and funding to act on it. Commissions like it are chronically under-resourced for a problem this size; fixing that is the highest-return investment we can make for ratepayers.
Modernize the grid — transmission, storage, and distribution upgrades are the most boring policy on offer, and the highest ROI we have for unlocking the clean power that’s already viable.
Keep every safe, clean power source on the table. I operated a Navy reactor for nine and a half years — done right, the physics works and the people running it know it.
Already law — Washington’s cap-and-invest program for the clean energy transition. I’ll defend it against raids on its funding.

pages.title: About – Stephen for District 31
paragraphs: I was born and raised in the Bay Area, California. My mom was a receptionist and my dad a machinist; they separated when I was young. I graduated from high school during the Great Recession and watched as the economy crumbled around us. In 2009 I was fortunate enough to go to college for my bachelor’s at UC Santa Barbara with the help of my family, and worked a part time job as a campus security guard.

When my grandfather was diagnosed with stage four lung cancer in 2013, I took a few weeks to visit with him. I was with him until the day he died. When I came home, the school wouldn’t refund the quarter — even knowing why I had left. A friend stepped in to help. Another got me a job at a froyo shop. I made up credits at community college, and returned to UC Santa Barbara in 2014 to finish my degree. Were it not for my friends and family I would not have been able to complete that degree. They taught me the importance of community.

After college I found jobs in my field were scarce. I worked at Office Depot, at Nordstrom, and as a security guard again, until 2015 when I joined the Navy. For nine and a half years I served my country as a nuclear reactor operator, deploying three times aboard the USS Theodore Roosevelt — once to the Middle East to assist the Kurds and our allies against ISIS, and twice more to the South China Sea for freedom of navigation operations.

I served alongside people doing hard work under hard conditions. Some of them were the most generous people I’ve known. Others showed me what stress can do when there’s nowhere for it to go. They all taught me that dignity and respect are practices, not feelings — they’re what you maintain under pressure, not what you have when it’s easy.

After my last deployment my wife agreed to move out to upstate New York with me, where we started our family. There I served the remainder of my term with the Navy and finished my Master of Public Administration in the summer of 2025. By fall I started a job as an HVAC technician, and we moved out to Washington and settled in Auburn to be closer to both of our families. They remind me why I still serve.

I am running for state House Representative because my service did not end when I hung up the uniform. I am running because my son deserves to grow up in a community that isn’t torn apart by outrage media, and neighbors who used to know each other. And I am running because I believe that you deserve to be treated with dignity and respect by the people you elect.
I’m running for the parents whose children did everything right — earning their bachelors, getting their masters, and are still unable to find a job, with no prospects of owning their own home.
I am running for the voter who has shown up for 50 years — at the polls, at the protests, in this room — who feels beyond tired.
And I am running for my son, who I want to inherit a Washington that is Evergreen, an economy that is fulfilling, and a democracy where his voice and the voices of all the children here are heard.
Paychecks that go further, schools that work, streets that are safe.
A representative who answers the phone and remembers the district’s name.
An affordable place to put down roots and a reason to stay.

pages.title: Representative Josh Penner | 31st Legislative District
paragraphs: Washington doesn't need more partisan warfare. We need discipline, data-driven oversight, and leaders who measure success by results.
Select an issue to see how Olympia's spending measures up against reality.
The 'Keeping Families Together Act' elevated standards for child removal so high that caseworkers were unable to rescue infants from lethal fentanyl-exposed environments.
Led the charge on the House floor to dismantle this deadly standard so our caseworkers can intervene proactively and save children's lives.
Fought SB 5167 to stop the legislature from shutting down Residential Habilitation Centers (RHCs) without adequate care facilities for the severely disabled in place.
Led the charge against SB 5925, fighting back against unchecked investigatory powers that would allow the Attorney General to bypass due process and burden local governments.
Fought SB 6309 to prevent Sound Transit from sidestepping local zoning laws and dodging financial accountability while holding billions of taxpayer dollars in debt.
Start with a rough thought. My tool helps you sharpen it into a real bill, shows you what Olympia has already tried, and I read every one.
Unfiltered updates from the front lines in Olympia. No spam, just the reality of what's happening in Washington State.
Join your neighbors across the 31st District
Your information is securely processed via Beehiiv and never shared.

pages.title: The Unacceptable Tragedy of State Neglect | Josh Penner
paragraphs: “ There has been some conversation about whether 50 children died in the last year or 90 children died. It doesn't matter if it's 50 or 90. We should be crawling out of our skin if it's one. ”
“ There has been some conversation about whether 50 children died in the last year or 90 children died. It doesn't matter if it's 50 or 90. We should be crawling out of our skin if it's one. ”

The debate on the House floor during the 2026 session marked one of the darkest moments in our state's history. We were not just discussing policy. We were arguing over the body count of our own failures.

The root of the crisis was the "Keeping Families Together Act" (KFTA). This law fundamentally broke our child welfare system. It elevated the standard for removing a child to "imminent physical harm." In practice, this meant our caseworkers could not rescue a child from a home littered with fentanyl unless they could prove immediate, physical injury.
We tied the hands of our protectors. We left children in toxic, lethal environments in the name of bureaucratic family preservation.
When the inevitable tragedies occurred, the legislature engaged in a sickening debate over the exact number of fatalities. I refused to let my colleagues hide behind a spreadsheet.
“ There has been some conversation about whether 50 children died in the last year or 90 children died. It doesn't matter if it's 50 or 90. We should be crawling out of our skin if it's one. ”
The opposition deflected. They defended the KFTA. They prioritized an extreme, academic view of child welfare over the visceral reality of babies dying from fentanyl poisoning.

I led the charge to dismantle this deadly standard. I fought to amend the law so our caseworkers could intervene proactively. When a child's environment becomes a drug den, the state must act immediately. We cannot wait for a fatality to justify our compassion.
This fight exposed a deep rot in Olympia. The extreme majority lost touch with basic human preservation.
I am stepping up to take Washington back. I am fighting to bring balance to Olympia.

We are the adults in the room. We demand a state where government executes the basics flawlessly. There is no duty more basic than protecting a vulnerable child from a lethal environment. We must stop the extremes from gambling with the lives of our youth.
We need common sense to dictate our laws, not radical ideology. We need accountability, action, and unyielding protection for the most vulnerable among us.
Stand with me. Join the coalition to protect our children and bring sanity back to our government.
Help us hold the line against bad policy and runaway spending.
Olympia passes complex utility mandates, withholds clear guidance, then lets local providers take the blame. The result is higher compliance costs and higher power bills for working families.
A Silent Killer in Our Living Rooms Every parent knows the drill. You watch your toddler's every move. You check the floor for small toys or stray pie...

pages.title: Budgeting Over Human Lives: Saving Disability Care | Josh Penner
paragraphs: “ Right now in two years we will not have the enhanced behavioral support... And I fear some of them (the profoundly disabled adults we care for) will die. ”
“ Right now in two years we will not have the enhanced behavioral support... And I fear some of them (the profoundly disabled adults we care for) will die. ”

The 2025 legislative session brought a grave crisis to the doorstep of our state. The majority party attempted to force the closure of critical Residential Habilitation Centers (RHCs). They targeted facilities that provide 24/7 care to our most profoundly disabled adults. This reckless plan ignored the harsh reality of our current infrastructure. It left vulnerable residents facing the terrifying prospect of homelessness or death.

The state lacked any viable community care alternative. This failure placed our most vulnerable neighbors in immediate danger. The opposition viewed these human beings as mere spreadsheet line-items. They prioritized irresponsible budgeting over the lives of Washington citizens. I saw the danger clearly, and I heard the cries for help from families who feared for their loved ones.

I stood on the House floor to address this systemic breakdown. I realized that this issue extended far beyond a single piece of legislation. The core problem involves a fundamental failure in our state's ability to execute basic functions. Closing these facilities without a safety net is an abdication of our moral duty.
“ Right now in two years we will not have the enhanced behavioral support... And I fear some of them (the profoundly disabled adults we care for) will die. ”

I fought this closure with every tool at my disposal. I worked tirelessly to stop the destruction of these essential facilities. We successfully killed the Senate version of the closure bill. My efforts forced the legislature to keep these facilities open. We ensured that no further closures could occur without a concrete, safe plan in place, fighting to protect the Rainier and Yakima Valley schools .
This victory belonged to the families and the residents. We proved that we can stand against reckless policy. We proved that we can protect those who cannot protect themselves.

Our work does not end with this legislative session. We must take Washington back. We need to bring balance to Olympia. I want a state where government executes the basics flawlessly. We need a government that builds, houses, and budgets with competence and care.

The extremes in our legislature continue to threaten our stability. We must reject the politics of convenience. We must reject the politics of neglect. I am committed to being the adult in the room. I will continue to advocate for common sense and fundamental stability. We must stop the extremes and start focusing on the essential duties of state government. We must protect the vulnerable and ensure our community remains strong.

pages.title: Stop the Tyranny: Protecting Washington's Small Businesses | Josh Penner
paragraphs: “ Mr. Speaker, hot air, like tyranny, will expand to the container it fills. ”
“ Mr. Speaker, hot air, like tyranny, will expand to the container it fills. ”
Olympia recently pushed legislation that would give the Attorney General’s Office unprecedented, unchecked power to demand endless records from small businesses and local city governments.
They didn’t offer to pay for the massive legal bills this would cause. They just expected you—the taxpayer and the business owner—to cover the cost of their investigations.
This isn't about reasonable accountability or standard legal practice. This is about enabling what amounts to a state-sponsored fishing expedition.

When a government agency is allowed to bypass established procedures under the Public Records Act, they can demand thousands of pages of documents without clear cause. For a massive corporation with an army of lawyers, that’s an inconvenience. For a local mom-and-pop shop or a small city council, it is an impossible financial burden.
It forces local job creators into bankruptcy just to prove they are innocent.

As I noted during the floor debate, the State of Washington is already equipped with all the necessary legal tools for proper, lawful investigation. Expanding this power doesn't make us safer—it merely lubricates existing tendencies toward government overreach.

If even a small percentage of state attorneys misuse this immense power, they risk ruining businesses and destroying livelihoods. The immense power of the State of Washington should never be used to compel our businesses into financial ruin without clear, verifiable evidence of wrongdoing.
I stood up and fought back against this legislation on the House floor because we cannot allow state lawyers to adopt an 'eye of Sauron' approach over our local communities.
I introduced and fought for multiple amendments designed to shield local budgets from these state demands and to put hard guardrails on the Attorney General's investigatory powers.

We must demand that our state government operates with strict accountability, complete transparency, and a fundamental respect for the taxpayers who fund it. We need leaders in Olympia who will protect the people building our economy, not bureaucrats looking to expand their own authority.

pages.title: Taxation Without Accountability: Reigning in Sound Transit | Josh Penner
paragraphs: “ This is government for the government, by the government. ”
“ This is government for the government, by the government. ”

Sound Transit operates as an unelected board hoarding billions in debt. Yet, they collect massive amounts of your property and sales taxes every single year. The 31st District pays more to Sound Transit than they pay to their own city governments, all while receiving a fraction of the services they were promised.

When Olympia tried to pass SB 6309, they sought to let Sound Transit bypass local zoning laws and dodge even more financial accountability. I challenged them directly on the House floor because this legislation represents everything wrong with how our state manages its regional transit authorities.
“ This is government for the government, by the government. ”

The struggle over SB 6309 highlighted the exact dangers of centralized power. During the debates, the tension between regional mandates and local autonomy became undeniable. Proponents of expanded authority ignored the voices of the very people they serve.

They treated our tax dollars as a blank check for their mismanaged mega-projects. The expansion of authority within regional bodies creates a dangerous precedent. When we allow centralized agencies to bypass local input and rewrite zoning laws to suit their own needs, we weaken the very foundation of our communities.

We deserve a transportation system that answers to taxpayers, not bureaucrats in Seattle. I have consistently challenged the Sound Transit narrative because we cannot afford to keep funding a system that operates without transparency.

I am fighting to bring accountability back to Olympia. We need an adult in the room to say "no" to unchecked expansion. We must demand that our state government operates with strict accountability and a fundamental respect for the taxpayers who fund it.
Stand with me to demand accountability. We must stop the extremes from funneling our money into ideological vanity projects and return local control to our communities.

pages.title: Elect John Bielka | WA State Rep, 31st LD (D)
paragraphs: Thank you to everyone who voted for me in the primary election. We had a strong showing, and I am truly grateful for your trust and support.
Our campaign is gaining momentum because voters want honest leadership, responsible budgeting, stronger infrastructure, safer communities, and practical solutions that make life more affordable.

Now we move forward to the general election. I am asking for your continued support—and for the support of your family, friends, and neighbors. Together, we can bring common sense, accountability, and real results to Olympia.
We’d love to have your support! Sign-up to get involved and join our campaign.

I’m running for State House because District 31 needs practical results — lower costs, less unnecessary regulation, a responsible budget, and faster delivery of transportation, housing, and flood-protection projects.
I support the Second Amendment and responsible gun ownership. I support small businesses, safer communities, and enough officers to respond when people need help.

I will be honest with voters, read the bills, show the math, and protect taxpayers from wasteful, overbuilt government projects. I’m not running to play politics. I’m running to do the work and make real progress.

pages.title: Priorities for the 31st LD — Elect John Bielka
paragraphs: Housing costs are squeezing working families, seniors, and young people trying to stay in their communities. We need more housing choices, faster permitting, and practical paths to ownership.
I support adding housing where roads, utilities, and services can support it, including ADUs, duplexes, townhomes, small multifamily housing, and nonprofit-led tiny home communities.

I also support allowing larger existing homes to be divided into separate condo-style ownership units where it can be done safely and responsibly. This could create more affordable ownership opportunities without always requiring new land, major infrastructure, or large apartment projects.
Permitting should be clear, timely, and predictable so good housing projects do not get stuck for years.
Bottom line: create more housing choices, reduce unnecessary delay, and help working families afford a place to own or rent
Healthcare should be easier to access, easier to understand, and more affordable for families. Too many people delay care because of cost, lack of appointments, or confusing bills.
My mother-in-law is in a nursing home, and we have friends who work as nurses. We see the pressure on patients, families, caregivers, and healthcare workers.
I support expanding access to primary care, mental health care, senior care, and cost-effective local clinics so people can get help before small problems become emergencies.
I also support price transparency, fewer surprise bills, and reforms that reduce costs without lowering quality.
Bottom line: make healthcare more affordable, support caregivers, reduce barriers to care, and focus on results people can actually feel.

Washington must live within a responsible budget and make sure taxpayer dollars deliver real results. Government should measure what works, fix what does not, and stop funding programs that fail to deliver.

I believe in maintaining roads, bridges, utilities, schools, and public buildings before small problems become expensive failures. I will also push for better control of project costs, schedules, and scope because delays and poor planning are hidden costs to taxpayers.
I will not support increased taxes until the Legislature prioritizes its spending choices. Governor Gregoire honestly observed that Washington has a spending problem, not a revenue problem.

Washington has had consistent revenue growth for the past 11 years. In that time, our state budget has grown 116%, while population has grown 13%. And we are always running a deficit. Some of that is due to changing how we pay for schools, but the Legislature has continually budgeted based on expected growth instead of actual receipts.

Even worse, when the Federal Government increased support during the Covid crisis, we made new expenditures, knowing that money would stop. Those funds should have been invested in critical needs, like bridges and stormwater management.

Every family, business and community knows it cannot spend more than it makes. Borrowing from tomorrow will finally collide with today. Acting otherwise risks those who rely on you. We need to honestly evaluate and choose better on how we spend taxpayers’ money and live within our means. When I am elected, I will tell you honestly whether any new proposed taxes meets this standard.
Bottom line: spend responsibly, measure results, and protect taxpayers from waste and delay.

District 31 depends on key transportation corridors for work, school, freight, farming, emergency response, and daily life. Congestion is not just an inconvenience — it adds time, fuel costs, delivery costs, and stress to families and businesses.

I support practical transportation fixes first: better incident response, improved signal timing, safer intersections, targeted chokepoint improvements, and stronger coordination between state and local roads.
Major projects should move forward only when they improve safety, reduce delays, and protect taxpayer dollars.
I also support reviewing better east-west connections so traffic is not simply pushed onto SR 162 and local roads that were not designed to carry that level of demand.
Bottom line: reduce delays, improve safety, keep freight moving, and make transportation dollars count.
Public safety is a basic responsibility of government. Families, businesses, and neighborhoods need officers who can respond quickly, investigate crime, and hold repeat offenders accountable.
I support recruiting and retaining well-trained officers, strong professional standards, and better coordination between law enforcement, prosecutors, and local communities.
I also support stronger behavioral health and crisis-response systems so police are not the only option when someone is in crisis.
Bottom line: support law enforcement, hold repeat offenders accountable, improve crisis response, and make our communities safer.
Flooding is not a partisan issue — it is a public safety, property, and infrastructure issue. Small cities cannot afford to keep paying for the same damage over and over.

I support proactive flood planning, including identifying weak berms, levees, culverts, and known flooding points before storms hit. I also support using Climate Commitment Act funding where appropriate to fix flooding problems, improve drainage, protect roads, and reduce long-term damage.
Emergency repairs should lead to permanent fixes so taxpayers do not pay twice.
Bottom line: prepare early, fix flooding problems, and protect homes, roads, and taxpayers.
Small businesses are the backbone of District 31. They need predictable rules, timely permits, and a state government that understands how delays and compliance costs affect jobs.
I support reducing red tape, making permitting more predictable, and expanding apprenticeships, trades, and CTE programs so young people can build careers and local businesses can hire locally.
I also support fair public contracting practices, including clear scopes, prompt payment, and realistic schedules so small contractors have a fair chance to compete.
Bottom line: support small businesses, train the next generation, and keep local jobs in our communities.
Tribal nations and tribal communities are an important part of District 31. I support partnerships built on respect, listening, sovereignty, and practical collaboration.
I volunteer as a CTE advisor for Chief Leschi Schools, and I believe strongly in education, workforce training, trades, and career pathways that help young people build a future close to home.
I also support clean water, fisheries, habitat restoration, and flood-control projects that improve public safety while protecting natural resources.
Bottom line: respect sovereignty, listen early, support students, protect fisheries, and work together on practical solutions.

I support regulations that protect safety, clean water, farmland, and the environment. But rules should be clear, measurable, and timely. Government should protect the public without turning every project into years of delay.

I will support practical permitting reform, including clear application checklists, firm review timelines, one lead contact for applicants, and concurrent agency review so projects are not passed from desk to desk.
I will also work to reduce duplicate studies, require agencies to report permit timelines, and focus regulations on measurable outcomes instead of unnecessary paperwork.
This matters for housing, roads, bridges, utilities, farms, small businesses, and flood-control projects. If a project meets the rules, it should get a timely yes or no.
Bottom line: protect people and the environment, reduce unnecessary delay, and make government deliver results taxpayers can afford.

I stand for the Second Amendment and responsible gun ownership. I will respect the rights of law-abiding gun owners while supporting practical, enforceable measures to keep firearms away from violent offenders, domestic abusers, and people who are legally prohibited from possessing them.

pages.title: Candidate Background — Elect John Bielka
paragraphs: A civil engineer running to deliver practical results and lower costs for District 31
My name is John Bielka. I am a civil engineer, public works leader, cattle farmer, father, husband, and community volunteer.

I spent my career building and fixing the roads, utilities, water systems, sewer systems, and flood-protection projects families depend on. After retiring from public works, I chose to focus full time on this campaign because I believe the 31st District deserves practical leadership in Olympia.
I understand rising costs, housing pressure, taxes, utility bills, small business, agriculture, and the frustration people feel when government creates more paperwork than results.
“I will not support unfunded mandates that shove costs onto cities and towns and end up raising local taxes or utility bills.” — John Bielka (D)
I am running as a Democrat, but I am independent-minded and practical.
I believe government should protect people and the environment, while also reducing unnecessary delays, paperwork, and costs that make housing, infrastructure, and everyday life more expensive.
I believe in environmental stewardship — but I believe regulations should be outcomes-based and measurable, not paperwork and delay.
If you want a representative who will read the bill, show the math, tell you the truth, and deliver results — I’m asking for your vote.

pages.title: Cindy Ryu
paragraphs: "Ryu is a reliable Democratic voice in Olympia with her top policy priorities as public education, climate, transit infrastructure, and small businesses. "
"Throughout her tenure, she helped pass a slate of progressive bills, including bills to strengthen voting processes, support professional licensing for undocumented Washingtonians..."

"During her time in the House, Ryu supported a number of affordable housing bills through her votes and sponsorships. She voted in favor of rent stabilization and co-sponsored a bill to promote transit-oriented housing developments."
Serving as your representative in the State Legislature since 2011, Cindy is ready to make sure District 32 is heard in the state Senate.

pages.title: Issues — cindyryu.com
paragraphs: Transportation Maintenance and Expansion

The cost of living in Washington is raising faster than wages. I want to make living in Washington more affordable for working families by increasing access to affordable childcare and reliable transportation .

I’ve spent my career fighting for fully funded public schools , because I believe every child deserves a high-quality education . From supporting smaller class sizes and early learning programs to paying teachers and staff fairly, I’ve worked to ensure every student has the resources and opportunities they need to succeed .

Some of my top priorities are expanding access to safe, affordable housing for all Washington families, supporting rent caps , creating first-time homebuyer programs , and speeding up construction . My leadership has focused on making homeownership and stable housing a reality for working families.
Our government should help small businesses succeed by providing tax credits, trade opportunities, and community investment without compromising on consumer and worker protections.

I have a track record of strengthening citizens’ rights against predatory corporate practices , because I believe consumer protections must always come first. From improving transparency and accountability to standing up to unfair lending and corporate abuse, I’ve worked to ensure Washingtonians are treated fairly and protected every step of the way.
I'm a proud advoacate of protecting reproductive rights , because these medical decisions should be made between patients and their doctors, not politicians or government officials.

As a city council member and mayor, I witnessed firsthand the importance of community policing and believe that, even amid complex challenges, we must prioritize both public safety and accountability in law enforcement .

We must protect our planet from climate change and safeguard the future for generations to come. I am committed to advancing renewable energy and growing Washington’s workforce in the green energy sector.
I’ve dedicated my career to advancing equity and opportunity in Washington, empowering communities that have long been left out and ensuring every resident has the tools to succeed.
Transportation Maintenance and Expansion

Having lived in multiple cities across the 32nd Legislative District for 40 years, I have a personal understanding of our community’s transportation needs and the importance of maintaining the infrastructure that keeps our cities moving.

pages.title: About — cindyryu.com
paragraphs: After serving in the state legislature, Cindy is ready to bring her leadership to make voice stronger in the Washington State Senate.

Cindy and her husband Cody have deep roots in their community. Cindy immigrated to Washington State in 1969 from Korea via Brunei and Manila, growing up in rural Thurston and small town Lewis Counties. They have lived and worked in, and raised their three children in north King and south Snohomish Counties since 1976. Cindy received a Bachelor of Science in microbiology and an MBA in operations management from the University of Washington, Seattle.

Cindy chairs the Technology, Economic Development and Veterans Committee, with jurisdiction over AI, tourism, under-represented communities, disaster preparedness and response, community resilience, broadband, and telecommunications. She also serves on Appropriations and Consumer Protection & Business committees.

While a Shoreline City Councilmember, Cindy served as Mayor, becoming the first Korean American woman mayor in America. In Shoreline, she served as President of both the Shoreline Chamber of Commerce and its Dollars For Scholars Chapter, helped improve numerous public parks, build its first City Hall and create Shoreline’s Green Business Program. In 2024-2025, Cindy served as President of Pacific Northwest Economic Region, bringing policy makers and industry together from 5 northwest states and 5 western Canadian provinces and territories.
Cindy has fought to increase funding for Washington’s public schools and she will continue working to ensure students have the resources they need to thrive.
Cindy has championed bills to protect comsumers from unfair business practices, predatory lending, and preventing copper wire theft.
Cindy fought to make sure millionaires pay their fair share in taxes to deliver public services while protecting working-class families
Across her career, Cindy has voted to increase wages for workers across the state and supported stronger worker protections, like paid family leave and basic labor standards.

pages.title: Vote Jesse Salomon
paragraphs: Since 2018, Jesse has worked tirelessly in the State Senate to ensure that every community in Washington has the resources it needs to thrive. He has led efforts to expand affordable housing, protect survivors of domestic violence, strengthen gun safety, and restore our natural environment—delivering real results for families across the state.

Jesse has fought back against federal overreach throughout his career. He has defended Washingtonians against Donald Trump’s attacks on reproductive care, public education, and other programs our families rely on, always prioritizing people over political pressure.

As Senate Local Government Committee Chair and a member of the Housing, Law and Justice and Rules Committees, Jesse pushes for practical solutions in Olympia. His experience spans public service and law—as a Shoreline City Councilmember and Deputy Mayor, a public defender, and a prosecutor protecting abused children—giving him the expertise and leadership to tackle the state’s toughest challenges.

As more people move to our region, addressing transportation challenges and traffic congestion has become increasingly important. Jesse was proud to help pass a $16 billion transportation package —one of the greenest and most transit-focused investments in Washington’s history.

Our forefathers created America because they did not want to be ruled by a king. Because of Trump’s actions, American has never been closer to having a king. I am very proud to say the Washington State Legislature has passed over 140 laws to help “Trump proof” our state!
Jesse sponsored legislation to make it easier for seniors to access property tax relief and worked extensively to expand housing supply and lower housing costs.

During his time in the Senate, Jesse has passed meaningful legislation every single year– from increasing access to affordable housing to strengthening gun safety laws and protecting our environment. He’s also passed legislation to protect our elections, ban fracking for natural gas, and preserve access to healthcare. He supported legislation that cuts taxes on small businesses and expands the Working Families Tax Credit.

pages.title: Issues — Vote Jesse Salomon
paragraphs: Washingtonians are facing soaring housing and rent prices, rising grocery bills, cuts to healthcare, and the ongoing impact of Donald Trump’s tariffs. Jesse believes that reducing costs for working people during these challenging times must be a top priority. He has sponsored legislation to make it easier for seniors to access property tax relief and worked extensively to expand housing supply and lower housing costs. He supported legislation that cuts taxes on small businesses and expands the Working Families Tax Credit.

Jesse has worked extensively to expand the supply of housing, including rental units, condominiums, cottage housing, and smaller “starter” homes that have long been missing from the market. More housing supply will help bring down costs, putting home ownership within reach for the young people and working families struggling to reach that goal.

He is proud to have written and passed Washington Senate Bills 5818 and 5412, which cut red tape and made it easier to build new housing. Jesse also supported landmark rent stabilization legislation, protecting renters from massive rent increases– helping them stay in their homes.

Jesse believes everybody in Washington State deserves affordable, high-quality healthcare, regardless of their income or where they live. While the State of Washington has made real progress, decisions in Washington, D.C. have pushed families backward. Trump’s cuts to Medicaid, new red tape, and the refusal of Congressional Republicans to extend federal health insurance subsidies have put thousands of Washingtonians at risk of losing coverage. Premiums have gone up, and too many people are forced to choose between medical care and paying for groceries or rent. This is unacceptable.
To protect care and bring down costs in Washington, these are Jesse’s three priorities:

Protect Washington families with progressive, sustainable revenue. Shielding our state from federal attacks on healthcare requires stable funding that does not fall on working families. Jesse proudly supports the ‘Millionaire’s Tax” because he believes the very wealthiest should pay their fair share so every family can get the medical care they need.

Hold for-profit healthcare systems accountable. We must do more to rein in high hospital and prescription drug costs. That means stronger rules publicizing costs, more oversight of corporate healthcare consolidation, and policies that put patients first.

Stand up for science-based public health. Jesse supports Washington’s partnership with California, Hawaii, and Oregon to coordinate vaccine and public-health guidance to ensure families receive reliable, science-driven health information. At a time when Trump and his lackeys are politicizing public health agencies, Washington must remain a leader in evidence-based care.
Jesse is committed to making sure every person in Washington can access affordable, dependable healthcare.

Jesse is 100% pro-choice and believes decisions about reproductive health care should be made by women and their doctors—not politicians. He supports access to reproductive health care for people across the economic spectrum, including access to birth control and breastfeeding supplies.

Jesse also believes medical providers who offer reproductive care must be protected under the law. After the 2022 overturning of Roe v. Wade, he worked with fellow legislators to develop a strategy to safeguard the right to choose in Washington and protect local doctors and nurses from out-of-state legal threats.

He sponsored Senate Bill 5400, which ensures that Washington medical providers cannot lose their licenses because of convictions in other states for providing care that is legal and consistent with Washington law and medical standards.
Jesse also strongly supports enshrining the right to reproductive care in Washington’s state constitution to ensure these protections remain secure for future generations.

Washington’s affordability crisis has made it increasingly difficult for many people to live and work in our communities, especially when it comes to buying a home. Jesse has worked extensively to expand the supply of housing, including rental units, condominiums, cottage housing, and smaller “starter” homes that have long been missing from the market.

He is proud to have written and passed Washington Senate Bills 5818 and 5412, which cut red tape and made it easier to build new housing. Jesse also supported landmark legislation to limit excessive rent increases, helping renters stay in their homes and providing greater stability for families across Washington.

Jesse believes everyone deserves to live in their community without fear or intimidation. While law enforcement must be able to do their jobs, ICE is operating in ways that violate constitutional protections and sow fear in our communities.

As a lawyer who spent most of his career defending constitutional rights, Jesse is deeply troubled by the impact of these practices. He has co-sponsored legislation to increase accountability and protect civil liberties, including bills that would prohibit ICE agents from wearing face coverings, require judicial warrants before entering sensitive locations such as schools, hospitals, and places of worship, and ensure employers notify workers when federal immigration audits are scheduled.

Public safety is critical to the health of our Washington communities. With the rise of drug use on our streets and the housing crisis causing more and more vulnerable people to wind up homeless, Jesse understands the balancing act required to address these issues to create safer neighborhoods while working to get people housed and clean.

The role of law enforcement and our judicial system is to keep violent offenders in check and keep people’s property and bodies safe. Police provide a necessary and valuable service for our communities often under dangerous conditions. However, Jesse also understands that someone experiencing a mental health crisis or suffering from addiction may require a more nuanced approach than just law enforcement or the community turning a blind eye. That is why he believes in implementing programs that address the root of these problems by providing mental health and drug treatment, creating housing options, and providing job training to get people on track. With the help of officers and specialists in these services, Jesse believes we can make real, long-term improvements that uplift our entire communities. Jesse believes that any agency, including law enforcement, needs to keep up with modern standards. He has supported reforms to better align police procedures and actions with the standards we expect and to create better ties with communities of color. His approach is simple: improve and reform — not tear down and destroy.

During his time on the Shoreline City Council, Jesse supported the Risk Assessment, Deterrence, and Referral (RADAR) Program, which increases the likelihood of de-escalation in police interactions with community members in mental health crisis. He has also supported investments in regional training academies so police cadets with families can complete their training closer to home, leading to a more diverse and representative police force. Jesse has also supported stronger accountability measures, like giving the Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission the authority to decertify officers who abuse the public’s trust, helping ensure higher standards in law enforcement.

When policy overcorrects, such as the 2021 Washington State v. Blake decision that virtually decriminalized all drugs across Washington, our communities face catastrophic consequences. That’s just one example of why Jesse has championed a balanced solution of enforcement and support that the Seattle Times called “the best chance for steering people to needed treatment.”
Gun violence remains far too common and continues to cause preventable tragedies in our communities. Jesse believes we must take common-sense steps to keep our communities safe.

He was the lead sponsor of Washington Senate Bill 6294, which requires individuals to successfully complete firearms safety training before obtaining a concealed pistol license, as well as Senate Bill 5231, a bipartisan bill that keeps guns out of the hands of domestic abusers.

Jesse also supported efforts to limit high-capacity magazines and strengthen background checks. In addition, he backs limits on open carry at school board meetings, protests, and similar public gatherings, as well as strong “red flag” laws that allow courts to temporarily remove firearms from individuals who pose a danger to themselves or others.

He also believes we must continue building the infrastructure that makes public transit more accessible and effective. That includes improving connections to the region’s expanding light rail system, such as faster and more reliable bus service that helps people easily get to and from stations.

Investing in education at every level is one of the most important commitments we can make to the next generation. Research consistently shows that early learning helps level the playing field, which is why Jesse supported Washington Senate Bill 5237 in 2021. The legislation provided hundreds of millions of dollars to expand access to preschool and childcare for low-income families. That investment is funded by Washington’s capital gains tax, which applies only to the top 0.25% of earners in the state.

Jesse also believes we must continue strengthening our public schools. That includes reducing class sizes, expanding tutoring and student support programs, and increasing access to free breakfast and lunch so every student can focus on learning.

Education is also key to workforce readiness. As career paths continue to evolve, Jesse believes students should have strong opportunities to pursue vocational and technical training alongside traditional four-year degree programs, ensuring every student can find a pathway that works for them.

The impacts of climate change are already being felt across the Pacific Northwest—from more frequent heat waves and droughts to worsening wildfire seasons and changing ocean conditions. Jesse knows that confronting climate change is one of the defining challenges of our time.

He was proud to sponsor the Washington Climate Commitment Act, landmark legislation that created a statewide carbon cap-and-invest program to reduce emissions while investing in clean energy and climate resilience. Jesse has also supported policies to accelerate Washington’s transition to clean energy and expand investments in wind and solar power and secured $500 million for stormwater treatment that will keep our water cleaner and protect salmon habitats.
He believes Washington must continue leading on climate solutions—protecting our environment, strengthening our economy, and building a more sustainable future.

pages.title: Meet Jesse — Vote Jesse Salomon
paragraphs: During his time in the Senate, Jesse has sponsored successful legislation that:
Made over the counter drugs more affordable
Passed a Millionaires Tax to make our tax code more fair

Before being elected to the Senate, Jesse served for seven years on the Shoreline City Council, including one year as Deputy Mayor. This city government experience has given him the background to personally understand neighborhood issues and best represent the cities of Edmonds, Lynnwood, Mountlake Terrace, NW Seattle, Shoreline, and Woodway.

Jesse worked for 15 years as a public defense attorney.
